XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Childcare

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad ar gyflwyno cynnig gofal plant Llywodraeth Cymru ym Mhowys? OQ64599
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the roll-out of the Welsh Government’s childcare offer in Powys? OQ64599

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn. Gan ddefnyddio'r cyllid ychwanegol y gwnaethon ni ei gyhoeddi yn gynharach eleni, rwyf wrth fy modd bod Powys yn gallu cyflwyno cam cyntaf y cynnig gofal plant a ariennir gan y Llywodraeth o 12.5 awr o ofal o ansawdd i bob plentyn dwy oed o fis Ionawr 2027.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for the question. Using the additional funding we announced earlier this year, I am delighted that Powys is able to roll out the first phase of the Government funded childcare offer of 12.5 hours of quality childcare for all two-year-olds from January 2027.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y diweddariad positif yna. Mae gwastad yn bryder yn y canolbarth fod pob dim yn mynd i'r ardaloedd trefol neu ddinesig. Byddai cael sicrwydd, felly, bydd ein hardaloedd gwledig yr un mor gymwys ac yn elwa o'r datblygiad pwysig yma ym maes gofal plant yn cael ei werthfawrogi. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that positive update. There is always a concern in mid Wales that everything goes to urban or city areas. An assurance, therefore, that our rural areas will also benefit from this important development in childcare would be appreciated. Thank you very much.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Ie, mae gofal plant hyblyg yn hanfodol, dwi'n meddwl, er mwyn cefnogi teuluoedd gyda chostau byw, a hynny ar draws Cymru ac ar draws pob ardal, er mwyn galluogi rhieni, fel roeddwn i'n sôn, i fanteisio ar fwy o gyfleoedd i weithio, i astudio, neu gynyddu eu horiau nhw, ac, wrth gwrs, er mwyn rhoi'r dechrau gorau hefyd i bob plentyn. Felly, rŷn ni'n datblygu'r cynnig gofal plant yna, a'r flaenoriaeth, fel roeddwn i'n sôn, oedd cynnig y 12.5 awr yma i bob plentyn ar draws Cymru—ac mae Powys yn dangos eu bod nhw'n mynd i fod yn gwneud cynnydd ar hynny yn fuan iawn, felly, dwi wrth fy modd. Ac mae disgwyl i'r system geisiadau yna agor i bob teulu ym Mhowys erbyn diwedd Tachwedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Yes, flexible childcare is crucial, I think, in order to support families with the cost of living, across Wales and in every area, in order to enable parents, as I mentioned, to take up more opportunities to work, to study or to increase their hours, and, of course, to give the best possible start to every child too. So, we are developing that childcare offer, and the priority, as I mentioned, was the offer of 12.5 hours for all children across Wales—and Powys has demonstrated that they will be making progress on that very soon, so I am delighted. And the applications system is expected to open to all families in Powys by the end of November.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. I welcome the principle of extending childcare, but there does seem to be a rather large gap between announcing an entitlement and families actually benefiting from it. Powys County Council has itself estimated that the parents of more than 1,000 young children in the county could be missing out on free or reduced-cost childcare. And, of course, in a county as large and rural as Powys, eligibility is only half the issue. There also has to be a suitable provider within a reasonable distance of where a family lives. So, Cabinet Minister, as you roll out this offer, what are you doing to ensure that Powys County Council not only identifies those families who are entitled to support, but has sufficient childcare provision for them actually to use it?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Rwy'n croesawu'r egwyddor o ehangu gofal plant, ond ymddengys bod bwlch eithaf mawr rhwng cyhoeddi hawl a theuluoedd yn elwa ohono mewn gwirionedd. Mae Cyngor Sir Powys ei hun wedi amcangyfrif y gallai rhieni mwy na 1,000 o blant ifanc yn y sir fod yn colli gofal plant am ddim neu ar gost ostyngedig. Ac wrth gwrs, mewn sir mor fawr a gwledig â Phowys, dim ond hanner y broblem yw cymhwysedd. Rhaid bod darparwr addas hefyd o fewn pellter rhesymol o ble mae teulu'n byw. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, wrth ichi gyflwyno'r cynnig hwn, beth rydych chi'n ei wneud i sicrhau bod Cyngor Sir Powys nid yn unig yn nodi'r teuluoedd sydd â hawl i gymorth, ond bod ganddo ddarpariaeth gofal plant digonol iddynt ei ddefnyddio mewn gwirionedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn atodol yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that supplementary question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are committed to ensuring that childcare expansion works for families in all parts of Wales, and that's including rural communities, where provision can be more dispersed and can be more fragile. So, we already have some flexibility in the system through guidance, through funding and local authority planning. But we are, as a part of this expansion programme, actively looking at what more can be done to ensure childcare hours and transport solutions and capital investment all respond to the specific needs of rural communities. So, local authorities use childcare sufficiency assessments and annual action plans to identify those gaps in provision, including those rural challenges, and we continue to support practical solutions, then, such as co-locations with schools and community hubs. We also recognise that childminders are really important as well in rural communities, and so we're working with partners, including Cwlwm, to support workforce development, business sustainability and provider capacity.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod ehangu gofal plant yn gweithio i deuluoedd ym mhob rhan o Gymru, ac mae hynny'n cynnwys cymunedau gwledig, lle gall y ddarpariaeth fod yn fwy gwasgaredig ac yn fwy bregus. Felly, mae gennym eisoes rywfaint o hyblygrwydd yn y system trwy ganllawiau, trwy gyllid a chynllunio gan awdurdodau lleol. Ond rydym yn edrych yn weithredol yn rhan o'r cynllun ehangu ar yr hyn y gellir ei wneud i sicrhau bod oriau gofal plant ac atebion trafnidiaeth a buddsoddiad cyfalaf oll yn ymateb i anghenion penodol cymunedau gwledig. Felly, mae awdurdodau lleol yn defnyddio asesiadau digonolrwydd gofal plant a chynlluniau gweithredu blynyddol i nodi bylchau yn y ddarpariaeth, gan gynnwys heriau gwledig, ac rydym yn parhau i gefnogi atebion ymarferol, fel cydleoli gydag ysgolion a hybiau cymunedol. Rydym hefyd yn cydnabod bod gwarchodwyr plant yn bwysig iawn mewn cymunedau gwledig, ac felly rydym yn gweithio gyda phartneriaid, gan gynnwys Cwlwm, i gefnogi datblygu'r gweithlu, cynaliadwyedd busnesau a chapasiti darparwyr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Caerphilly Post Office

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa asesiad y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'i wneud o effaith cau swyddfa bost Caerffili? OQ64598
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What assessment has the Cabinet Minister made of the impact of the closure of Caerphilly post office? OQ64598

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae gwasanaethau swyddfeydd post yn chwarae rôl hanfodol wrth gefnogi cymunedau. Mae'r materion hyn, wrth gwrs, wedi'u cadw'n ôl o fewn cylch cyfrifoldeb Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol, ac mae'r Llywodraeth honno wedi datgan mai ei nod yw cadw cymaint o ganghennau a gwasanaethau â phosibl.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Post office services play a vital role in supporting communities. These matters, of course, are reserved and are the responsibility of the UK Government, and that Government has stated that their aim is to retain as many branches and services as possible.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, can I thank you for your response? I, along with the leader of Caerphilly County Borough Council, have taken part in direct meetings with the Post Office to secure a suitable replacement in the town centre, but we are encountering a wall of excuses. The reason given by the Post Office as to why alternative sites are unsuitable do not stack up, because the excuse is that they are simply unsuitable—one site, across the road from the post office that had been there, to my knowledge, for at least 73 years, was because there is unsuitable parking. Minister, can I please ask you if you could commit to making direct representations to the Post Office executive to challenge these reasons for site rejections? We do need transparency on when the town centre will finally get its service back. I do feel that if the local Senedd Member—sorry, one of the local Senedd Members—and the leader of council can't get answers, I'm sure, they may listen to you, Minister. I know that I certainly would. [Laughter.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, a gaf i ddiolch i chi am eich ymateb? Rwyf i, ynghyd ag arweinydd Cyngor Bwrdeistref Sirol Caerffili, wedi cymryd rhan mewn cyfarfodydd uniongyrchol gyda Swyddfa'r Post i sicrhau lle amgen addas yng nghanol y dref, ond rydym yn wynebu wal o esgusodion. Nid yw'r rheswm a roddwyd gan Swyddfa'r Post i egluro pam y mae safleoedd amgen yn anaddas yn dal dŵr, oherwydd yr esgus yw eu bod, yn syml iawn, yn anaddas—un safle, ar draws y ffordd i'r swyddfa bost a fu yno am o leiaf 73 mlynedd hyd y gwn i, y rheswm a roddwyd oedd bod y parcio'n anaddas. Weinidog, a gaf i ofyn i chi ymrwymo i wneud sylwadau uniongyrchol i weithrediaeth Swyddfa'r Post i herio'r rhesymau hyn dros wrthod safleoedd? Mae angen tryloywder ynglŷn â phryd y bydd canol y dref yn cael ei wasanaeth yn ôl o'r diwedd. Rwy'n teimlo os nad yw'r Aelod Senedd lleol—mae'n ddrwg gennyf, un o'r Aelodau Senedd lleol—ac arweinydd y cyngor yn gallu cael atebion, efallai y gwnânt wrando arnoch chi, Weinidog. Rwy'n gwybod y buaswn i'n sicr yn gwneud. [Chwerthin.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lindsay, am y cwestiwn. Yn gyntaf oll, rwy'n moyn cydnabod y pryder pan fo cymuned yn colli gwasanaethau. Dwi'n gwybod bod nifer ohonom ni wedi gweld hyn yn ein cymunedau dros y blynyddoedd, ar y stryd fawr o ran banciau yn benodol, ac, yn yr un modd, weithiau, pan fo gwasanaeth post yn dod i ben.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Lindsay, for the question. First of all, I want to acknowledge the concern when a community loses services. I know a number of us have seen this in our communities over the years, on the high street in terms of banks specifically, and, in the same way, sometimes, when post office services come to an end.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I just want to let the Member know that I actually met with the Post Office, with Post Office Ltd, yesterday. Again, as I said, they provided reassurance to maintain the network, as is their duty. I'm pleased to say that the Post Office Ltd confirmed to me that they have—because I did raise this topic specifically around post office services in Caerphilly—received expressions of interest to run the post office service in Caerphilly, and these are now currently being reviewed. So, that process, from expressions of interest to being, typically, open, takes up to six months. So, I hope that that will give your constituents assurance that we, hopefully, will see that post office service resume in your area.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Hoffwn roi gwybod i'r Aelod fy mod wedi cyfarfod â Swyddfa'r Post Cyf ddoe. Unwaith eto, fel y dywedais, rhoddasant sicrwydd y byddant yn cynnal y rhwydwaith, fel sy'n ddyletswydd arnynt. Mae'n bleser gennyf ddweud—gan fy mod wedi codi'r mater hwn yn benodol yng nghyd-destun gwasanaethau swyddfa bost yng Nghaerffili—fod Swyddfa'r Post Cyf wedi cadarnhau wrthyf eu bod wedi derbyn datganiadau o ddiddordeb i redeg gwasanaeth y swyddfa bost yng Nghaerffili, ac mae'r rhain yn cael eu hystyried ar hyn o bryd. Felly, mae'r broses honno, o ddatgan diddordeb i fod ar agor yn cymryd hyd at chwe mis fel arfer. Felly, rwy'n gobeithio y bydd hynny'n rhoi sicrwydd i'ch etholwyr y byddwn, gobeithio, yn gweld gwasanaeth swyddfa bost yn ailddechrau yn eich ardal chi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Minister for the answer there. The other concern that people are passing to me in terms of post office closures—whether it's Caerphilly or throughout the constituency—is, once the post office closes, it's the lack of being able to get ID, identification; it's the additional services that the post office uniquely provides to communities. I appreciate what you said on Caerphilly there, but what about other parts of Wales and my constituency that have lost that service, and now people are unable to get identification, because of simple things like the proofreading, the assistance, that the post office provides? What help can the Welsh Government provide to constituents there?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i'r Gweinidog am ei hateb. Y pryder arall y mae pobl yn ei adrodd wrthyf o ran cau swyddfeydd post—boed hynny yng Nghaerffili neu ledled yr etholaeth—yw, pan fydd y swyddfa bost yn cau, nid oes modd cael ID, dulliau adnabod, a'r gwasanaethau ychwanegol nad oes neb ond y swyddfa bost yn eu darparu i gymunedau. Rwy'n derbyn yr hyn a ddywedoch chi am Gaerffili yno, ond beth am rannau eraill o Gymru a fy etholaeth sydd wedi colli'r gwasanaeth hwnnw, a nawr nid oes modd i bobl gael dull adnabod, oherwydd pethau syml fel prawfddarllen, y cymorth, y mae'r swyddfa bost yn ei ddarparu? Pa gymorth y gall Llywodraeth Cymru ei ddarparu i etholwyr yno?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Rwy'n cydnabod yn llwyr y gofidiau yma. Dwi'n siŵr, eto, eu bod nhw'n gyfarwydd i ni i gyd. Mae'r gwasanaethau yn rhai hanfodol iawn i'n cymunedau ni, yn enwedig i bobl sydd, efallai, ddim yn medru defnyddio, neu does yna ddim argaeledd, trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus ac yn y blaen, er mwyn mynd i'r dref nesaf. Maen nhw'n rhan bwysig o'n canol trefi a'n strydoedd mawr, a dyna yw safbwynt y Llywodraeth, yn sicr.

Wrth gwrs, eto, dyw materion sy'n ymwneud â swyddfeydd post ddim wedi eu datganoli i Weinidogion Cymru. Fel y soniais i yn yr ateb cynharach, mae ymrwymiad Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol i swyddfeydd post yn cynnwys cynlluniau i gadw maint y rhwydwaith fel y mae, ac mae hynny'n golygu chwilio wedyn am fusnesau newydd i gynnig y gwasanaeth pan fydd swyddfeydd post unigol yn cau. Ond mae hefyd yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i leoli swyddfeydd post yng nghanol trefi, lle y bo'n bosibl. Achos, fel roeddwn i'n dweud, dwi'n cytuno—rŷn ni'n gwybod, onid ydyn ni, fod presenoldeb swyddfa bost yn cynyddu nifer yr ymwelwyr â stryd fawr, yn ogystal, wrth gwrs, â darparu'r gwasanaethau hanfodol yna.

Mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i archwilio'r opsiynau yna i adfywio canol ein trefi, felly, wrth gwrs yn gysylltiedig â'n gwaith ni o ran y tasglu canol trefi rŷn ni wedi ei sefydlu. Felly, dwi'n siŵr y byddai sicrhau bod swyddfeydd post yn gallu bod yn rhan o strydoedd mawr bywiog yn gallu bod yn rhan o'r gwaith yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I fully recognise those concerns. I'm sure that they are familiar to us all. Those services are crucial to our communities, particularly for people who perhaps can't use public transport or there is no transport available to take them to the next town. They are an important part of our town centres and high streets, and that is the Government's view, most certainly.

But, again, issues related to post offices are not devolved to Welsh Ministers. As I mentioned in an earlier response, the UK Government's commitment to post offices includes plans to retain the size of the network as it is, and that means looking for new businesses to offer those services when individual post offices close. But it also includes a commitment to locate post offices in town centres, where possible. Because, as I said, I agree—we know that post offices increase the number of visitors to the high street, as well as providing those crucial services.

Our programme for government does include a commitment to look at those options to rejuvenate our town centres, and that links to our work in terms of the town-centre taskforce that we've established. So, I'm sure that ensuring that post offices can be part of vibrant high streets could be part of that work too.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Beth mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn ei wneud i fynd i'r afael â'r heriau gwledig unigryw sy'n gysylltiedig â thlodi plant yng Ngheredigion Penfro? OQ64603
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What is the Cabinet Minister doing to tackle the unique rural challenges associated with child poverty in Ceredigion Penfro? OQ64603

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rŷn ni'n cydnabod bod teuluoedd mewn ardaloedd gwledig yn gallu wynebu rhwystrau ychwanegol, gan gynnwys mynediad mwy cyfyngedig at gyflogaeth, gwasanaethau a thrafnidiaeth, ynghyd â chostau uwch. Dyna pam mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i ddeddfu ar gyfer prawfesur gwledig, er mwyn helpu i sicrhau canlyniadau gwell i blant sy'n byw mewn tlodi mewn ardaloedd gwledig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We recognise that rural families can face additional barriers, including restricted access to employment, services and transport, as well as higher costs. That is why our programme for government includes a commitment to legislate for rural-proofing, helping to deliver better outcomes for children living in poverty in rural areas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Cabinet Minister. A 2023 report by the Bevan Foundation found that Ceredigion ranks second in child poverty levels across Wales, with Pembrokeshire not far behind. Crisis has also highlighted that many families in my constituency face significant gaps between their incomes and essential living costs, leaving them at greater risk of poverty and financial hardship.

Whilst child poverty exists across Wales, it's often less visible in rural and coastal constituencies. One example in my constituency is Aberporth, a beautiful and vibrant village that many Members might know as a holiday destination, but also where one in four children live in poverty. In these communities, community action can make a real difference to people's lives—for example, the incredible range of activities that are run from the renovated Aberporth village hall that provide not just practical support, but friendships and social support that are invaluable to people.

So, will the Cabinet Minister consider what more can be done to strengthen our community infrastructure as part of your efforts to address child poverty?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Canfu adroddiad 2023 gan Sefydliad Bevan fod Ceredigion yn ail o ran lefelau tlodi plant ledled Cymru, gyda sir Benfro heb fod ymhell ar eu holau. Mae Crisis hefyd wedi tynnu sylw at y ffaith bod llawer o deuluoedd yn fy etholaeth i'n wynebu bylchau sylweddol rhwng eu hincwm a'u costau byw hanfodol, gan eu gadael mewn mwy o berygl o dlodi a chaledi ariannol.

Er bod tlodi plant yn bodoli ledled Cymru, mae'n aml yn llai gweladwy mewn etholaethau gwledig ac arfordirol. Un enghraifft yn fy etholaeth i yw Aberporth, pentref hardd a bywiog y mae llawer o'r Aelodau'n ei adnabod o bosibl fel cyrchfan gwyliau, ond hefyd lle mae un o bob pedwar o'r plant yn byw mewn tlodi. Yn y cymunedau hyn, gall gweithredu cymunedol wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i fywydau pobl—er enghraifft, yr ystod anhygoel o weithgareddau sy'n cael eu rhedeg o neuadd bentref Aberporth wedi'i hadnewyddu sy'n darparu nid yn unig cymorth ymarferol, ond cyfeillgarwch a chefnogaeth gymdeithasol sy'n amhrisiadwy i bobl.

Felly, a wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet ystyried beth arall y gellir ei wneud i gryfhau ein seilwaith cymunedol fel rhan o'ch ymdrechion i fynd i'r afael â thlodi plant?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Dwi'n meddwl bod defnyddio'r enghraifft yna y gwnaethoch chi ddefnyddio fanna o ran Aberporth, rhywle dwi'n siŵr bod nifer ohonom ni wedi ymweld ag e—lle hyfryd, lle mor bert, ond mae yna rywbeth cudd, yntefe? Ac mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cydnabod bod tlodi gwledig yn aml yn llai gweladwy na thlodi sydd yn ein trefi a'n dinasoedd ni, ond dyw e ddim yn llai real. Rŷn ni'n benderfynol fel Llywodraeth o sicrhau bod plant a theuluoedd mewn cymunedau gwledig yn cael y cymorth sydd ei angen arnynt.

Dylai pob plentyn yng Nghymru, lle bynnag maen nhw'n byw, gael yr un cyfle i lwyddo. Felly, rŷn ni eisiau sicrhau bod ein hymrwymiad o ran ein polisïau yn arddangos hynny, a'n bod ni'n cymryd hynny i ystyriaeth ym mhopeth rŷn ni'n ei wneud. Felly, rŷn ni'n cydnabod bod llawer o deuluoedd yn wynebu heriau penodol, fel rydw i wedi sôn yn gynharach, o ran enillion is a chostau teithio ac ynni uwch, ac yn y blaen, ac mae'n anodd hefyd weithiau cael mynediad at y gwasanaethau a'r cymorth maen nhw eu hangen.

Felly, dyna pam rŷn ni wedi sicrhau y cymorth yma i deuluoedd ledled Cymru yn ein pecyn cymorth trechu tlodi, sydd yn werth bron £5 miliwn, sy'n cynnwys y cymorth penodol yna i gymunedau gwledig a chanolfannau, fel yr oedd yr Aelod yn sôn amdanynt, i gynllunio a helpu'r rhai sy'n wynebu'r pwysau ariannol mwyaf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. I think that using that example you used there in terms of Aberporth, somewhere that I'm sure a number of us have visited—a very beautiful place, a pretty place, but there is something hidden, isn't there? And Welsh Government recognises that rural poverty quite often is less visible than poverty in our towns and cities, but it's no less real. We are determined as a Government to ensure that children and families in rural communities have the support they need.

Every child in Wales, wherever they may live, should have the same opportunity to succeed. So, we want to ensure that our commitment in terms of our policies shows that, and that we take that into consideration in everything that we do. So, we recognise that many families are facing specific challenges, as I've mentioned earlier, in terms of lower pay and higher transport and energy costs, and so on, and also sometimes it's difficult to access the services and support they require.

So, that's why we have ensured that support is available to families throughout Wales in our tackling poverty programme, which is worth about £5 million and includes that specific support for rural communities and centres, such as the Member mentioned, to plan and to help those who are facing the greatest financial pressures.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you to Anna for the question. Deputy First Minister, on 22 September the First Minister told the Senedd that Cynnal was going to be piloted and it is happening, yet your programme for government says that you will 'seek to' pilot Cynnal. The distinction there really matters, Minister, because 'we're going to' is a commitment, while 'seek to' is not. So, for families in Ceredigion Penfro, I have two straightforward questions: will Ceredigion Penfro be included in the Cynnal pilot? And on your childcare commitment, on what date will families in Ceredigion Penfro be able to access the allocated funded hours per week? Families need to know not just what this Government intends to do, but when they will actually receive the support. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i Anna am y cwestiwn. Ddirprwy Brif Weinidog, ar 22 Medi dywedodd y Prif Weinidog wrth y Senedd fod Cynnal yn mynd i gael ei dreialu ac mae'n digwydd, ond mae eich rhaglen lywodraethu'n dweud y byddwch chi'n mynd ati ('seek to') i dreialu Cynnal. Mae'r gwahaniaeth yno'n wirioneddol bwysig, Weinidog, oherwydd mae 'rydym ni'n mynd i' yn ymrwymiad, ond nid yw 'seek to'. Felly, i deuluoedd yng Ngheredigion Penfro, mae gennyf ddau gwestiwn syml: a fydd Ceredigion Penfro yn cael ei gynnwys yng nghynllun peilot Cynnal? Ac ar eich ymrwymiad gofal plant, ar ba ddyddiad y bydd teuluoedd yng Ngheredigion Penfro yn gallu cael mynediad at yr oriau wythnosol a ariennir? Mae angen i deuluoedd wybod nid yn unig beth y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn bwriadu ei wneud, ond pryd y byddant yn cael y cymorth mewn gwirionedd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to clarify the reason why it says 'seek to pilot': it's because there's a very important decision that needs to be made by the UK Treasury, because what we don't want to do with Cynnal is make families worse off. We want to make them better off. So, that means the UK Treasury has to give a benefit and tax disregard. We heard some encouraging signs in an interview with Andy Burnham during the Labour conference on that. It's something, of course, that I've been pressing on with the UK Treasury, and so of course has the Cabinet Minister for Finance, because we want them to allow us to—. We have the powers to pilot the payment, but what we don't have are the powers over that tax and benefit disregard. So, that's why we are saying 'seek to pilot', because we don't have—. We wouldn't want to do something if we didn't have that assurance from UK Treasury that it wouldn't make families worse off. 

We are preparing to implement that pilot. We've commissioned an expert team to help lead on that design, thinking about then, obviously, again, the monitoring and evaluation. We want it to be effective. We've already met four times, and we're meeting again in a few weeks' time. It's been an intense piece of work. It's an intense process because we do want to make sure that we can get this payment out to families—a payment that has proven so successful in Scotland in lowering rates of child poverty—out to children who are in need as soon as we possibly can.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn egluro'r rheswm pam y mae'n dweud 'seek to pilot': mae hynny oherwydd bod angen i Drysorlys y DU wneud penderfyniad pwysig iawn, oherwydd yr hyn nad ydym am ei wneud gyda Cynnal yw gadael teuluoedd yn waeth eu byd. Rydym am eu gwneud yn well eu byd. Felly, mae hynny'n golygu bod angen i Drysorlys y DU ganiatáu diystyriad o ran budd-daliadau a threth. Clywsom arwyddion calonogol mewn cyfweliad ag Andy Burnham yn ystod cynhadledd y Blaid Lafur. Wrth gwrs, mae hyn yn rhywbeth rwyf wedi bod yn pwyso ar Drysorlys y DU yn ei gylch, ac felly hefyd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid, oherwydd rydym am iddynt ganiatáu i ni—. Mae gennym bwerau i lywio'r taliad, ond nid oes gennym bwerau dros y diystyriad treth a budd-daliadau. Dyna pam ein bod yn dweud 'seek to pilot', oherwydd nid oes gennym—. Ni fyddem eisiau gwneud rhywbeth os na chawn sicrwydd gan Drysorlys y DU na fyddai'n gwneud teuluoedd yn waeth eu byd.

Rydym yn paratoi i weithredu'r cynllun peilot hwnnw. Rydym wedi comisiynu tîm arbenigol i helpu i arwain ar ei luniad, gan feddwl wedyn unwaith eto am y monitro a'r gwerthuso. Rydym eisiau iddo fod yn effeithiol. Rydym eisoes wedi cyfarfod bedair gwaith, ac rydym yn cyfarfod eto ymhen ychydig wythnosau. Mae wedi bod yn waith dwys. Mae'n broses ddwys am ein bod eisiau gwneud yn siŵr y gallwn gael y taliad hwn i deuluoedd—taliad sydd wedi profi mor llwyddiannus yn yr Alban yn lleihau cyfraddau tlodi plant—i blant mewn angen cyn gynted ag y gallwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â thlodi plant? OQ64596
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What action is the Welsh Government taking to tackle child poverty? OQ64596

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tackling child poverty is central to our programme for government. We are already delivering on our commitments on free school meals and the childcare offer, as well as developing our Cynnal child payment. Our new child poverty strategy will include clear, measurable targets to improve outcomes for children and families.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae mynd i'r afael â thlodi plant yn ganolog i'n rhaglen lywodraethu. Rydym eisoes yn cyflawni ein hymrwymiadau ar brydau ysgol am ddim a'r cynnig gofal plant, yn ogystal â datblygu ein taliad plant Cynnal. Bydd ein strategaeth tlodi plant newydd yn cynnwys targedau clir, mesuradwy i wella canlyniadau i blant a theuluoedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. In my constituency of Fflint Wrecsam, there are currently 12,786 children living in poverty. In Caia Park, where I live, we have one of the highest levels of deprivation, not just in the constituency, but one of the highest levels across Cymru. We all know that children who grow up in poverty are far more likely to find themselves categorised as not in education, employment or training later in life, becoming trapped in a cycle of poverty. It's vital that we break that cycle, isn't it, and ensure that every child gets a fair chance to succeed.

We know that progress is possible. The only nation in the UK where child poverty rates are improving is Scotland. And Scotland acts as an example to all of us in Cymru in terms of what can be achieved when Governments have the tools to do more for their own people. The Scottish child payment and their additional powers on welfare are making a tangible difference there. So, my question in many ways follows on from Paul Marr's, which you very eloquently just answered, in terms of the progress the Government is making in implementing Cynnal, our Welsh child payment pilot, and ensuring that under a Plaid Cymru Government, child poverty statistics finally start moving in the right direction.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Yn fy etholaeth i, Fflint Wrecsam, ar hyn o bryd mae 12,786 o blant yn byw mewn tlodi. Ym Mharc Caia, lle rwy'n byw, mae gennym un o'r lefelau uchaf o amddifadedd, nid yn unig yn yr etholaeth, ond un o'r lefelau uchaf ledled Cymru. Rydym oll yn gwybod bod plant sy'n tyfu i fyny mewn tlodi yn llawer mwy tebygol o gael eu categoreiddio fel rhai nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant yn ddiweddarach mewn bywyd, a chael eu dal mewn cylch o dlodi. Mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn torri'r cylch hwnnw, onid yw, ac yn sicrhau bod pob plentyn yn cael cyfle teg i lwyddo.

Gwyddom fod cynnydd yn bosibl. Yr Alban yw'r unig genedl yn y DU lle mae cyfraddau tlodi plant yn gwella. Ac mae'r Alban yn esiampl i bob un ohonom yng Nghymru o ran yr hyn y gellir ei gyflawni pan fydd gan Lywodraethau'r offer i wneud mwy dros eu pobl eu hunain. Mae taliad plant yr Alban a'u pwerau ychwanegol ym maes lles yn gwneud gwahaniaeth pendant yno.Felly, mae fy nghwestiwn mewn sawl ffordd yn dilyn ymlaen o un Paul Marr, y gwnaethoch ei ateb yn huawdl iawn, o ran y cynnydd y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud ar weithredu Cynnal, ein cynllun peilot taliadau plant yng Nghymru, a sicrhau bod ystadegau tlodi plant o'r diwedd yn dechrau symud i'r cyfeiriad cywir o dan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We are, as I said, already making progress on the preparation of that implementation of the Cynnal pilot, the Welsh child payment. We have heard views and evidence on how such a payment could make a real tangible difference to families, so we want to make sure that we design a pilot that can demonstrate that. That expert group I was referring to earlier, which I'm co-chairing with Steffan Evans from the Bevan Foundation, is meeting regularly, as I said, to help with that design, help with the implementation, so it launches on a real sound and evidence-based footing as soon as that preparation is complete.

On the tax and benefit disregards, I met with Baroness Sherlock, who's Minister of State in the Department for Work and Pensions, to discuss our ambitions around child poverty more broadly, and also the Cynnal payment. She has agreed to work with us to explore how we can ensure those payments do not impact on tax and benefits. And also, on the implementation piece, it's around how we can share DWP data as well, for delivery purposes. So, our officials are working together to take this forward.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fel y dywedais, rydym eisoes yn gwneud cynnydd ar baratoi gweithrediad y cynllun peilot Cynnal, taliad plant Cymru. Rydym wedi clywed barn a thystiolaeth ar sut y gallai taliad o'r fath wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i deuluoedd, felly rydym eisiau gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn llunio cynllun peilot sy'n gallu dangos hynny. Mae'r grŵp arbenigol y cyfeiriais ato yn gynharach ac a gyd-gadeiriaf gyda Steffan Evans o Sefydliad Bevan yn cyfarfod yn rheolaidd, fel y dywedais, i helpu gyda'r gwaith o'i gynllunio, i helpu gyda'i weithrediad, felly mae'n lansio ar sail tystiolaeth gadarn cyn gynted ag y bydd y gwaith paratoi hwnnw wedi'i gwblhau.

Ar y diystyriadau treth a budd-daliadau, cyfarfûm â'r Farwnes Sherlock, sy'n Weinidog Gwladol yn yr Adran Gwaith a Phensiynau, i drafod ein huchelgeisiau ynghylch tlodi plant yn ehangach, a hefyd y taliad Cynnal. Mae hi wedi cytuno i weithio gyda ni i archwilio sut y gallwn sicrhau nad yw'r taliadau hynny'n effeithio ar dreth a budd-daliadau. Ac ar ei weithrediad, mae'n ymwneud â sut y gallwn rannu data'r Adran Gwaith a Phensiynau hefyd, at ddibenion cyflawni. Felly, mae ein swyddogion yn gweithio gyda'i gilydd i symud hyn yn ei flaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mannau Gwyrdd Cymunedol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Community Green Spaces

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddiogelu mannau gwyrdd cymunedol yng Nghasnewydd ac Islwyn? OQ64574
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What action is the Welsh Government taking to protect community green spaces in Newport and Islwyn? OQ64574

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Obviously, our community green spaces matter for people, for nature and the places where people live. We are investing in programmes that protect and improve them, including in Newport and Islwyn. I want to build on that work, particularly in communities where access to good-quality green space is most limited.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn amlwg, mae ein mannau gwyrdd cymunedol yn bwysig i bobl, i natur a'r lleoedd lle mae pobl yn byw. Rydym yn buddsoddi mewn rhaglenni sy'n eu diogelu a'u gwella, gan gynnwys yng Nghasnewydd ac Islwyn. Rwyf am adeiladu ar y gwaith hwnnw, yn enwedig mewn cymunedau lle mae mynediad at fannau gwyrdd o ansawdd da yn fwyaf cyfyngedig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thanks so much for your response. Cabinet Secretary, over the summer, I met up with a group of residents in Newport who are concerned that they are poised to lose the only community green space in their area, and a plan has been drawn up by Newport City Council. Constituents of mine, particularly dog walkers, children and families, make full use of a parcel of land just off Ruskin Avenue in Rogerstone North, but that could soon come to an end if the local authority rubber-stamps the plan to turn the community green space into an allotment site. To be clear, no-one is against allotment sites or developments, but not only would that take away a vital community asset, it's simply not the right site, with fears about even more traffic in the area, as residents are already experiencing and facing that sort of problem.

Cabinet Minister, more than 200 residents have signed a petition calling for the site in Rogerstone North to be ruled out. I've written to the council myself highlighting the residents' concerns and calling for the site to be dropped, and the decision now rests with the local authority. So, will you join me in putting pressure on Newport council to protect this community green space by removing it from the authority's allotment plans?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am eich ymateb. Ysgrifennydd y Cabinet, yn ystod yr haf, cyfarfûm â grŵp o drigolion yng Nghasnewydd sy'n pryderu eu bod ar fin colli'r unig fan gwyrdd cymunedol yn eu hardal, ac mae cynllun wedi'i lunio gan Gyngor Dinas Casnewydd. Mae rhai o fy etholwyr, yn enwedig y rhai sy'n mynd â'u cŵn am dro, plant a theuluoedd, yn gwneud defnydd llawn o ddarn o dir oddi ar Ruskin Avenue yng Ngogledd Tŷ-du, ond gallai hynny ddod i ben yn fuan os bydd yr awdurdod lleol yn cymeradwyo'r cynllun i droi'r man gwyrdd cymunedol yn safle rhandiroedd. I fod yn glir, nid oes neb yn gwrthwynebu safleoedd rhandiroedd na datblygiadau, ond nid yn unig y byddai hynny'n dileu ased cymunedol hanfodol, yn syml iawn nid dyma'r safle cywir, gyda phryderon ynghylch mwy fyth o draffig yn yr ardal, lle mae trigolion eisoes yn profi ac yn wynebu problem o'r fath.

Weinidog Cabinet, mae mwy na 200 o drigolion wedi llofnodi deiseb yn galw am eithrio'r safle yng Ngogledd Tŷ-du. Rwyf wedi ysgrifennu at y cyngor fy hun yn tynnu sylw at bryderon y trigolion ac yn galw am ddiystyru'r safle, a mater i'r awdurdod lleol yw'r penderfyniad bellach. Felly, a wnewch chi ymuno â mi i roi pwysau ar gyngor Casnewydd i ddiogelu'r man gwyrdd cymunedol hwn trwy ei dynnu allan o gynlluniau'r awdurdod ar gyfer rhandiroedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for raising this issue. I am aware, actually, of the concerns that residents have raised on this particular issue. You will also know that this is a matter for Newport City Council; it wouldn't be appropriate for me to intervene in what is and should be a local decision. But I think the wider principle here is important. Communities need both accessible green spaces and opportunities to grow food. But it is important, of course, that those local decisions have to reflect the value that people place on these spaces, and access to nature shouldn't depend, really, on where you live. I want more people to have good-quality green spaces close to home, particularly, as I said in my initial answer, where access is currently poorest.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am godi'r mater hwn. Rwy'n ymwybodol o'r pryderon y mae trigolion wedi'u codi ar y mater penodol hwn mewn gwirionedd. Fe fyddwch chi hefyd yn gwybod mai mater i Gyngor Dinas Casnewydd ydyw; ni fyddai'n briodol i mi ymyrryd mewn mater sydd, ac a ddylai fod yn benderfyniad lleol. Ond rwy'n credu bod yr egwyddor ehangach yma'n bwysig. Mae angen mannau gwyrdd hygyrch a chyfleoedd i dyfu bwyd ar gymunedau. Ond mae'n bwysig, wrth gwrs, fod yn rhaid i'r penderfyniadau lleol hynny adlewyrchu'r gwerth y mae pobl yn ei roi ar y mannau hyn, ac ni ddylai mynediad at fyd natur ddibynnu ar ble rydych chi'n byw. Rwyf am i fwy o bobl gael mannau gwyrdd o ansawdd da yn agos at adref, yn enwedig, fel y dywedais yn fy ateb cychwynnol, lle na cheir mynediad da at fannau o'r fath ar hyn o bryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, Wales needs both renewable energy and secure domestic food production. Welsh planning policy already gives considerable weight to protecting our best and most versatile agricultural land. Can you explain how the protection works alongside the Government's drive for renewable energy, so that we increase green generation without unnecessarily losing our most productive farmland?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae angen ynni adnewyddadwy a chynhyrchiant bwyd domestig diogel ar Gymru. Mae polisi cynllunio Cymru eisoes yn rhoi pwyslais sylweddol ar ddiogelu ein tir amaethyddol gorau a mwyaf amlbwrpas. A allwch chi esbonio sut y mae'r diogelwch yn gweithio ochr yn ochr ag ymgyrch y Llywodraeth i sicrhau ynni adnewyddadwy, fel ein bod yn cynyddu cynhyrchiant gwyrdd heb golli ein tir fferm mwyaf cynhyrchiol yn ddiangen?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for the question. Obviously it's about striking the right balance, isn't it? We know that there is a demand for energy, we know that there is a demand for food, and consequently there will be, sometimes, conflicting demand for land. The planning system is there to try and protect the integrity of those demands in a way that strikes the right balance. Sometimes, planning authorities get it right, other times, maybe, people will disagree, and that's the nature of the situation that we're facing.

You will know—and I am straying into the territory of other Ministers here—that work is ongoing to look at planning policy, particularly in relation to energy infrastructure. There is also work happening on a new national energy strategy for us here in Wales. I will entrust that work to my Cabinet colleagues, and I am confident that they will get it right and also confident, of course, that all Members here in the Senedd will have an opportunity to scrutinise that when the time is right.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y cwestiwn. Yn amlwg mae'n ymwneud â tharo'r cydbwysedd cywir, onid yw? Rydym yn gwybod bod galw am ynni, rydym yn gwybod bod galw am fwyd, ac o ganlyniad bydd y galw am dir yn gwrthdaro o bryd i'w gilydd. Mae'r system gynllunio yno i geisio diogelu uniondeb y galwadau hynny mewn ffordd sy'n taro'r cydbwysedd cywir. Weithiau, mae awdurdodau cynllunio'n ei wneud yn iawn, ac ar adegau eraill efallai, bydd pobl yn anghytuno, a dyna natur y sefyllfa rydym yn ei hwynebu.

Fe fyddwch chi'n gwybod—ac rwy'n crwydro i diriogaeth Gweinidogion eraill yma—fod gwaith yn mynd rhagddo i edrych ar bolisi cynllunio, yn enwedig mewn perthynas â seilwaith ynni. Mae gwaith hefyd yn digwydd ar strategaeth ynni genedlaethol newydd i ni yma yng Nghymru. Byddaf yn ymddiried y gwaith hwnnw i fy nghyd-Aelodau yn y Cabinet, ac rwy'n hyderus y byddant yn ei wneud yn iawn, ac yn hyderus hefyd, wrth gwrs, y bydd yr holl Aelodau yma yn y Senedd yn cael cyfle i graffu ar hynny ar yr adeg iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We are very similar in the questioning, Lyn, so I'll try and skirt around some of the other parts of it.

Cabinet Minister, it's not just community green spaces at risk in Casnewydd, but also agricultural land. Currently, plans see 578 acres of farmland given over to solar development at the Candwr and Craig y Perthi sites. Residents have raised serious concerns about flood risk, traffic, landscape damage and impact on wildlife, including the important lapwing habitat on the Gwent levels, particularly around Bishton, which is their only site. What cumulative assessment has the Government made of the impact that these developments will have on food production, biodiversity and local flood risk? And does the Cabinet Minister believe that removing hundreds of acres of agricultural land is compatible with the Government's stated commitment to food security?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae ein cwestiynau'n debyg iawn, Lyn, felly fe geisiaf gynnwys rhai o'r rhannau eraill ohono.

Weinidog Cabinet, nid mannau gwyrdd cymunedol yn unig sydd dan fygythiad yng Nghasnewydd, ond tir amaethyddol hefyd. Ar hyn o bryd, mae cynlluniau'n darparu ar gyfer defnyddio 578 erw o dir fferm at ddibenion datblygu ynni solar yn safleoedd Candwr a Chraig y Perthi. Mae preswylwyr wedi codi pryderon difrifol ynghylch y risg o lifogydd, traffig, difrod i'r dirwedd ac effaith ar fywyd gwyllt, gan gynnwys cynefin pwysig y gornchwiglen ar wastadeddau Gwent, yn enwedig o amgylch Trefesgob, sef yr unig safle sydd ganddi. Pa asesiad cronnol y mae'r Llywodraeth wedi'i wneud o'r effaith y bydd y datblygiadau hyn yn ei chael ar gynhyrchiant bwyd, bioamrywiaeth a'r risg leol o lifogydd? Ac a yw'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn credu bod cael gwared ar gannoedd o erwau o dir amaethyddol yn gydnaws ag ymrwymiad datganedig y Llywodraeth i ddiogeledd bwyd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, thank you for the question. As you say, it's similar to the question that has been asked, and I feel that the answer may well be similar as well. But it is about striking that balance, I think, and, as I say, the planning system should, when it functions properly, take all of those considerations in the round and, hopefully, bring forward the right balance. But we are looking at planning policy in this energy space and we are working as well on the new energy strategy for Wales, much of which will not only deal with solar, but with the additional infrastructure that goes with some of these projects.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, diolch am y cwestiwn. Fel y dywedwch, mae'n debyg i'r cwestiwn sydd wedi'i ofyn, ac rwy'n teimlo y gallai'r ateb fod yn debyg hefyd. Ond mae'n ymwneud â tharo'r cydbwysedd hwnnw, rwy'n meddwl, ac fel y dywedais, dylai'r system gynllunio, pan fydd yn gweithredu'n iawn, ystyried yr holl bethau hynny yn eu cyfanrwydd, a sicrhau'r cydbwysedd cywir, gobeithio. Ond rydym yn edrych ar bolisi cynllunio yn y cyd-destun ynni ac rydym hefyd yn gweithio ar y strategaeth ynni newydd i Gymru, y bydd llawer ohoni nid yn unig yn ymdrin ag ynni solar, ond â'r seilwaith ychwanegol sy'n gysylltiedig â rhai o'r prosiectau hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Access to green spaces and nature is so important to our physical and mental well-being. The Road to Nature project in Newport is a great example of what can be done, and the incredible work of the Friends of the Road to Nature group, Newport City Council and the wider community has absolutely transformed what was a real criminal dumping ground for rubbish a few years ago, and that's now a haven for wildlife. Biodiversity is absolutely thriving there, and willow emerald damselflies were recorded for the first time in recent weeks, following the completion of a pond dipping area. This area is a real shining example of a community working together for nature restoration. So, will the Welsh Government commit to supporting and funding more projects like this in Casnewydd Islwyn, as well as other parts of Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae mynediad at fannau gwyrdd a natur mor bwysig i'n lles corfforol a meddyliol. Mae'r prosiect Ffordd at Natur yng Nghasnewydd yn enghraifft wych o'r hyn y gellir ei wneud, ac mae gwaith anhygoel grŵp Cyfeillion y Ffordd at Natur, Cyngor Dinas Casnewydd a'r gymuned ehangach wedi trawsnewid yn llwyr yr hyn a oedd yn dir dympio sbwriel troseddol go iawn ychydig flynyddoedd yn ôl, ac sydd bellach yn hafan i fywyd gwyllt. Mae bioamrywiaeth yn ffynnu yno, a chofnodwyd mursennod gwyrdd yr helyg am y tro cyntaf yn ystod yr wythnosau diwethaf, ar ôl cwblhau ardal pyllau dipio. Mae'r ardal hon yn enghraifft wych iawn o gymuned sy'n gweithio gyda'i gilydd ar gyfer adfer natur. Felly, a wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru ymrwymo i gefnogi ac ariannu mwy o brosiectau fel hyn yng Nghasnewydd Islwyn, yn ogystal â rhannau eraill o Gymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing attention to that particular scheme. I always believe that this kind of work is most effective when you empower local communities to take action like that, and, of course, we have backed that commitment with practical investment through Local Places for Nature, for example, because that scheme alone has created or improved thousands of green spaces and pollinator sites across Wales. In Newport and Caerphilly particularly, 28 community garden packages were delivered in the last year, creating nature gardens, orchards, food-growing areas, but wildlife habitats as well. Another 70 nature gardens are planned by the end of this year.

So, there's a lot happening, backed up by the £16 million that the Government has allocated to Local Places for Nature this year. It's very commendable, the work that's happening, and what we really want to see is how we can replicate that as widely as possible across the whole of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am dynnu sylw at y cynllun penodol hwnnw. Rwyf bob amser yn credu bod y math hwn o waith yn fwyaf effeithiol pan fyddwch chi'n grymuso cymunedau lleol i weithredu yn y ffordd honno, ac wrth gwrs, rydym wedi cefnogi'r ymrwymiad hwnnw gyda buddsoddiad ymarferol drwy Lleoedd Lleol ar gyfer Natur, er enghraifft, oherwydd mae'r cynllun hwnnw ynddo'i hun wedi creu neu wella miloedd o fannau gwyrdd a safleoedd pryfed peillio ledled Cymru. Yng Nghasnewydd a Chaerffili yn arbennig, cyflwynwyd 28 pecyn gardd gymunedol yn ystod y flwyddyn ddiwethaf, gan greu gerddi natur, perllannau, ardaloedd tyfu bwyd, a chynefinoedd bywyd gwyllt hefyd. Mae 70 o erddi natur eraill wedi'u cynllunio erbyn diwedd eleni.

Felly, mae llawer yn digwydd, wedi'i gefnogi gan y £16 miliwn y mae'r Llywodraeth wedi'i ddyrannu i Lleoedd Lleol ar gyfer Natur eleni. Mae'r gwaith sy'n digwydd yn ganmoladwy iawn a'r hyn rydym eisiau ei weld yn fawr yw sut y gallwn ailadrodd hynny mor eang â phosibl ar draws Cymru gyfan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Farmers in Carmarthenshire have reported Green GEN Cymru contractors arriving on their land without warning, with one recent incident reportedly requiring police attendance. This is causing real anxiety and frustration among farming families. Will the Minister raise these reports urgently with the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy and stand up within Government for the rural communities affected? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae ffermwyr yn sir Gaerfyrddin wedi dweud bod contractwyr Green GEN Cymru wedi dod ar eu tir heb rybudd, gydag un digwyddiad diweddar yn galw am bresenoldeb yr heddlu yn ôl y sôn. Mae hyn yn achosi pryder a rhwystredigaeth wirioneddol ymhlith teuluoedd ffermio. A wnaiff y Gweinidog godi'r adroddiadau hyn ar frys gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni a sefyll o fewn y Llywodraeth dros y cymunedau gwledig yr effeithir arnynt? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing our attention to that. I'm always concerned when there are any circumstances that require police attendance and police involvement. There's a certain way of doing things, and I think decent courtesy means that that should always be adhered to. I won't be drawn on commenting on any specifics, because I'm sure you can understand that I'd be straying into difficult territory.

But we do expect all developments planned in Wales to have regard to all relevant planning policy, to be sensitively designed and implemented to avoid and to definitely minimise impacts, at least on communities and the environment, but also to maximise the benefits, because I think there are two sides to this coin. When you get it right, it releases a lot of opportunities economically, et cetera, but when you get it wrong, then those are the risks that sometimes appear.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am dynnu ein sylw at hynny. Rwyf bob amser yn pryderu pan fydd unrhyw amgylchiadau'n galw am bresenoldeb yr heddlu ac ymwneud yr heddlu. Mae yna ffordd benodol o wneud pethau, ac rwy'n credu ei bod yn weddus cadw at hynny bob amser. Ni wnaf sylwadau ar unrhyw fanylion, oherwydd rwy'n siŵr y gallwch ddeall y buaswn yn gwyro i dir anodd.

Ond rydym yn disgwyl i bob datblygiad a gynllunnir yng Nghymru ystyried yr holl bolisi cynllunio perthnasol, i gael eu cynllunio a'u gweithredu'n sensitif er mwyn osgoi ac yn sicr i leihau effeithiau, ar gymunedau a'r amgylchedd fan lleiaf, ond hefyd i wneud y mwyaf o'r manteision, oherwydd rwy'n credu bod dwy ochr i'r geiniog yn y fan hon. Pan fyddwch chi'n ei gael yn iawn, mae'n rhyddhau llawer o gyfleoedd yn economaidd ac ati, ond pan fyddwch chi'n ei gael yn anghywir, dyna lle mae'r risgiau'n ymddangos weithiau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, that isn't really a role of mine within my portfolio. Clearly, it has a relevance to the energy Minister and it will have a relevance to the planning Minister as well. So, maybe you'd like to direct your question to them when the opportunity arises.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, nid yw'r swyddogaeth honno yn fy mhortffolio i mewn gwirionedd. Yn amlwg, mae'n berthnasol i'r Gweinidog ynni a bydd hefyd yn berthnasol i'r Gweinidog cynllunio. Felly, efallai yr hoffech ofyn eich cwestiwn iddynt hwy pan ddaw cyfle i chi wneud hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Deputy Presiding Officer. Firstly, Minister, I want to say 'diolch' to you too for your recent announcements, finally injecting some common sense into Labour's ridiculously rigid nitrate vulnerable zones rules. It's of course welcome and long overdue, as are advance payments for the basic payment scheme and the sustainable farming scheme after such a difficult summer.

But bringing forward that money does not give farmers a penny more overall, and it does not address the downward trajectory of the basic payment scheme. Lawfully, we are all, of course, aware that you have to bring down BPS payments, but it is in your power, Minister, as to how much. Many are struggling on the 60 per cent of the BPS original 2025 value. Now dropping it to just 40 per cent would literally signal the end of most family farms in Wales. As I am, you must be aware that the majority of the 51 per cent remaining on the BPS are those small family farms that you claim to want to protect. Pushing ahead with this cut, with SFS remaining wholly unsuitable, inflexible and unworkable, is playing literally Russian roulette with their livelihoods. Minister, you need to make the SFS workable, and fast, and you need to put protections in place to help those that remain on the BPS. So, would you consider dropping the BPS by just 1 per cent, as opposed to the further 20 per cent, unless of course you do want to be the Minister responsible for the genuine end of family farms across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Yn gyntaf, Weinidog, rwyf am ddiolch i chi hefyd am eich cyhoeddiadau diweddar, gan chwistrellu rhywfaint o synnwyr cyffredin o'r diwedd i mewn i reolau parthau nitradau gwirion o anhyblyg Llafur. Wrth gwrs, mae croeso mawr i hynny ac mae'n hen bryd ei wneud, fel y mae taliadau ymlaen llaw ar gyfer cynllun y taliad sylfaenol a'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy ar ôl haf mor anodd.

Ond nid yw talu'r arian hwnnw ymlaen llaw yn rhoi ceiniog yn fwy i ffermwyr yn gyffredinol, ac nid yw'n mynd i'r afael â thrywydd ar i lawr y cynllun taliad sylfaenol. Yn gyfreithlon, rydym i gyd yn ymwybodol wrth gwrs fod yn rhaid i chi ddod â thaliadau cynllun y taliad sylfaenol i lawr, ond mae maint y gostyngiad o fewn eich gallu chi i'w reoli, Weinidog. Mae llawer yn cael trafferth ar y 60 y cant o werth gwreiddiol cynllun y taliad sylfaenol 2025. Nawr byddai ei ostwng i ddim ond 40 y cant yn llythrennol yn ddiwedd ar y rhan fwyaf o ffermydd teuluol yng Nghymru. Rhaid eich bod yn ymwybodol, fel finnau, fod y mwyafrif o'r 51 y cant sy'n dal i fod ar gynllun y taliad sylfaenol yn ffermydd teuluol bach yr honnwch eich bod eisiau eu diogelu. Mae gwthio ymlaen â'r toriad hwn, gyda'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn parhau i fod yn gwbl anaddas, anhyblyg ac anymarferol, yn rhoi bywoliaeth pobl mewn perygl. Weinidog, mae angen ichi wneud y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn ymarferol, ac yn gyflym, ac mae angen ichi roi amddiffyniadau ar waith i helpu'r rhai sy'n aros ar gynllun y taliad sylfaenol. Felly, a fyddech chi'n ystyried gostwng cynllun y taliad sylfaenol 1 y cant yn unig, yn hytrach na'r 20 y cant pellach, oni bai wrth gwrs eich bod am gael eich adnabod fel y Gweinidog sy'n gyfrifol am roi diwedd ar ffermydd teuluol ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm under no illusion about the difficult transition that we're on at the minute, from the legacy BPS programme through to the new sustainable farming scheme. It's a journey that we will continue to travel on. You said that the SFS is wholly inflexible. Well, I'd like to think that some of the decisions and announcements that I've made of late shows that we can make it flexible and more workable for more farmers, so we will continue to do that. I will not entertain dropping the transition by just 1 per cent, but I am of course considering making the SFS truly more accessible to as many farmers as possible.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nid wyf o dan unrhyw gamargraff ynglŷn â'r cyfnod pontio anodd rydym ynddo ar hyn o bryd, o raglen etifeddol cynllun y taliad sylfaenol i'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy newydd. Mae'n daith y byddwn yn parhau arni. Fe ddywedoch chi fod y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn gwbl anhyblyg. Wel, hoffwn feddwl bod rhai o'r penderfyniadau a'r cyhoeddiadau a wneuthum yn ddiweddar yn dangos y gallwn ei wneud yn hyblyg ac yn fwy ymarferol i fwy o ffermwyr, felly byddwn yn parhau i wneud hynny. Nid wyf am ystyried gostwng lefel y cyllid 1 y cant yn unig, ond rwy'n ystyried gwneud y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn fwy hygyrch i gynifer o ffermwyr â phosibl wrth gwrs.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I hope you're more than considering it because it's absolutely completely unworkable, and you know that as well as I do. Not only is dropping the BPS funding by 1 per cent the right thing to do, but by not doing that and pushing ahead with this 20 per cent cut, you're putting our Welsh heritage, our Welsh culture and Welsh language at risk, as well as our national security. You said all the right things in opposition, Minister, didn't you? But now you seem to be struggling to say them and do them as the Minister. I know you've agreed with me in the past that the BPS trajectory needs to be a much more gradual, tapering trajectory—your words, not mine. Now you're in Government as the Minister able to do this, you're backtracking. You said in black and white in this Chamber that you thought that it should be a more just transition—again, your words. So, tell me: will you do it?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gobeithio eich bod yn gwneud mwy na'i ystyried, gan ei fod yn gwbl anymarferol, ac rydych chi'n gwybod hynny cystal â minnau. Nid yn unig mai gostwng lefel cyllid y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy 1 y cant yw'r peth iawn i'w wneud, ond drwy beidio â gwneud hynny a bwrw ymlaen â'r toriad o 20 y cant, rydych chi'n peryglu ein treftadaeth Gymreig, ein diwylliant Cymreig a'n hiaith Gymraeg, yn ogystal â'n diogelwch gwladol. Roeddech chi'n dweud yr holl bethau cywir pan oeddech yn yr wrthblaid, Weinidog, onid oeddech? Ond ymddengys eich bod nawr yn ei chael hi'n anodd eu dweud a'u gwneud fel y Gweinidog. Gwn eich bod wedi cytuno â mi yn y gorffennol fod angen i lwybr cynllun y taliad sylfaenol fod yn llwybr llawer mwy graddol—eich geiriau chi, nid fy rhai i. Gan eich bod bellach yn y Llywodraeth fel y Gweinidog sy'n gallu gwneud hyn, rydych chi'n torri'ch gair. Fe ddywedoch chi mewn du a gwyn yn y Siambr hon eich bod yn credu y dylai fod yn bontio tecach—unwaith eto, eich geiriau chi. Felly, dywedwch wrthyf: a fyddwch chi'n ei wneud?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
'Just transition' is exactly what we are trying to achieve here. You say that we've done nothing; we've committed £1 billion over the coming three years to farming to make sure that those farmers who aren't sure about coming on board with the SFS can see that there actually is a quantum of funding there that they can access, that they can utilise, to make their businesses and their farms more resilient. Now, some will choose not to do that and I appreciate that. My job is to make sure that as many people as possible who wish to come on that journey can do so. I'm focused on doing that because that is the just transition that we need to see.

But it isn't only about money as well, of course. We have introduced the review into red tape, which will be, hopefully, a great benefit to farmers who are grappling with the amount of paperwork that they're dealing with. You mentioned the control of agricultural pollution changes. We have been pragmatic, we have been practical, and, where we can do that, we will do that. But, ultimately, we are on this journey transitioning into the sustainable farming scheme and we need to keep our focus on getting there.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
'Pontio teg' yw'r union beth y ceisiwn ei gyflawni yma. Rydych chi'n dweud nad ydym wedi gwneud unrhyw beth; rydym wedi ymrwymo £1 biliwn i ffermio dros y tair blynedd nesaf i sicrhau y gall y ffermwyr hynny nad ydynt yn siŵr ynglŷn ag ymuno â'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy weld bod cwantwm o gyllid yno y gallant gael mynediad ato, y gallant ei ddefnyddio, i wneud eu busnesau a'u ffermydd yn fwy gwydn. Nawr, bydd rhai'n dewis peidio â gwneud hynny, ac rwy'n derbyn hynny. Fy swydd i yw sicrhau y gall cymaint o bobl â phosibl sydd am ddod ar y daith honno wneud hynny. Rwy'n canolbwyntio ar wneud hynny gan mai dyna'r pontio teg y mae angen i ni ei weld.

Ond mae'n ymwneud â mwy nag arian yn unig, wrth gwrs. Rydym wedi cyflwyno'r adolygiad i fiwrocratiaeth, a fydd, gobeithio, o fudd mawr i ffermwyr sy'n ei chael hi'n anodd ymdopi â'r holl waith papur. Fe sonioch chi am newidiadau i reoliadau llygredd amaethyddol. Rydym wedi bod yn bragmatig, rydym wedi bod yn ymarferol, a lle gallwn wneud hynny, byddwn yn gwneud hynny. Ond yn y pen draw, rydym ar y daith hon yn pontio i'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy, ac mae angen inni gadw ein ffocws ar gyrraedd yno.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, you're putting family farms in Wales at risk, Minister, by saying that. I hope that you do recognise that, currently, on the SFS, people cannot get on it whether they want to or not.

I'd like to bring back to what Sarah Edwards, one of my colleagues, has just asked you in the Chamber. I, too, am aware of the extremely worrying circumstance that Green GEN Cymru surveyors appear to be arriving unannounced on farms to survey land, with huge machinery, and, not only that, they are not even adhering to their own biosecurity measures, with no checks in place to ensure that they are. This is genuinely concerning. This is not about whether you agree with windfarms or not, Minister. Most of these farms have had bovine TB or are at high risk of it. This is not a theoretical concern either; the High Court has already found Green GEN lacking in terms of their biosecurity measures. Without the right measures in place here, there is a real risk of disease like TB being spread farm to farm, and I'm not even mentioning the other environmental concerns that the people of the Towy valley have. Don't you agree with me, Minister, that we cannot have a situation where rural communities in west Wales have to spend hundreds of thousands of pounds to ask a court to help them to merely protect their own farms? Farmers need protection in place. They need support on this, Minister. Green GEN Cymru and contracted surveyors need to adhere to the rules to protect our farms. Will you work with the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy to ensure this happens, please, and perhaps even visit the Towy valley to meet with the communities there that are so concerned? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, rydych chi'n peryglu ffermydd teuluol yng Nghymru, Weinidog, drwy ddweud hynny. Rwy'n gobeithio eich bod yn cydnabod, ar hyn o bryd, na all pobl ymuno â'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy p'un a ydynt eisiau gwneud hynny ai peidio.

Hoffwn ddychwelyd at yr hyn y mae Sarah Edwards, un o fy nghyd-Aelodau, newydd ei ofyn i chi yn y Siambr. Rwyf innau hefyd yn ymwybodol o'r sefyllfa hynod frawychus lle mae syrfewyr Green GEN Cymru yn ôl pob golwg yn mynd i ffermydd yn ddirybudd i arolygu tir, gyda pheiriannau enfawr, ac nid yn unig hynny, nid ydynt hyd yn oed yn cadw at eu mesurau bioddiogelwch eu hunain, heb unrhyw wiriadau ar waith i sicrhau eu bod yn gwneud hynny. Mae hyn yn peri pryder gwirioneddol. Nid oes a wnelo hyn â ph'un a ydych chi'n cytuno â ffermydd gwynt ai peidio, Weinidog. Mae'r rhan fwyaf o'r ffermydd hyn wedi cael neu mewn perygl mawr o gael TB buchol. Nid pryder damcaniaethol yw hwn chwaith; mae'r Uchel Lys eisoes wedi canfod bod mesurau bioddiogelwch Green GEN yn ddiffygiol. Heb y mesurau cywir ar waith yma, mae perygl gwirioneddol y bydd clefyd fel TB yn lledaenu o fferm i fferm, ac nid wyf yn sôn am y pryderon amgylcheddol eraill sydd gan bobl dyffryn Tywi. Onid ydych chi'n cytuno â mi, Weinidog, na allwn gael sefyllfa lle mae'n rhaid i gymunedau gwledig yng ngorllewin Cymru wario cannoedd o filoedd o bunnoedd i ofyn i lys eu helpu i ddiogelu eu ffermydd eu hunain? Mae angen amddiffyniadau ar ffermwyr. Mae angen cymorth arnynt yn hyn o beth, Weinidog. Mae angen i Green GEN Cymru a syrfewyr dan gontract lynu wrth y rheolau er mwyn diogelu ein ffermydd. A wnewch chi weithio gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni i sicrhau bod hyn yn digwydd, os gwelwch yn dda, ac ymweld â dyffryn Tywi efallai i gyfarfod â'r cymunedau yno sydd mor bryderus? Diolch.
