XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I won't get drawn on particular court cases, et cetera—you'll understand that I can't comment on those—but you make a very valid point about biosecurity measures, and I will write to the company and others to make sure that they are reminded of their responsibility particularly to respect those.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Nid wyf am drafod achosion llys penodol, ac yn y blaen—fe fyddwch yn deall na allaf wneud sylwadau ar y rheini—ond rydych chi'n gwneud pwynt dilys iawn ynglŷn â mesurau bioddiogelwch, ac fe ysgrifennaf at y cwmni ac eraill i sicrhau eu bod yn cael eu hatgoffa o'u cyfrifoldeb penodol i barchu'r rheini.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Vikki Howells.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Labour spokesperson, Vikki Howells.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, over lunch today we both attended WWF Cymru's briefing on the implications of extreme weather events such as wildfire and flooding, where we heard from speakers including representatives of the fire service and the farming sector. A key takeaway from that session for me was the vital role that nature-based solutions have to play in protecting communities and farm businesses from the impacts of climate change-related weather events. Given the shared commitments of our parties to increase the use of nature-based solutions across Government action, I'm wondering what steps you might intend to take to mainstream their use in the coming months. Both WWF Cymru and the Fire Brigades Union have come forward with funding proposals to ensure Wales is more resilient and better prepared for extreme weather impacts, and a key element of this proposal is seeking commitment to an extreme weather resilience fund that could look to inject tens of millions of new money into the expansion of preventative spend on nature-based solutions. We're at that time of year when everyone is talking about the budget, so, as those conversations go on, will you commit to making it a priority to expand nature-based solution investment within your portfolio?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, dros ginio heddiw, fe wnaethom ein dau fynychu sesiwn friffio WWF Cymru ar oblygiadau digwyddiadau tywydd eithafol fel tanau gwyllt a llifogydd, lle clywsom gan siaradwyr yn cynnwys cynrychiolwyr o'r gwasanaeth tân a'r sector ffermio. Un o'r pethau allweddol i mi eu dysgu yn y sesiwn honno oedd y rôl hanfodol y mae atebion ar sail ar natur yn ei chwarae yn diogelu cymunedau a busnesau fferm rhag effeithiau digwyddiadau tywydd sy'n gysylltiedig â newid hinsawdd. O ystyried ymrwymiadau cyffredin ein pleidiau i gynyddu'r defnydd o atebion ar sail natur ar draws gweithgarwch y Llywodraeth, rwy'n meddwl tybed pa gamau y bwriadwch eu cymryd i brif ffrydio eu defnydd yn y misoedd nesaf. Mae WWF Cymru ac Undeb y Brigadau Tân wedi cyflwyno cynigion ariannu i sicrhau bod Cymru'n fwy gwydn ac yn fwy parod ar gyfer effeithiau tywydd eithafol, ac elfen allweddol o'r cynnig hwn yw ceisio ymrwymiad i greu cronfa wydnwch rhag tywydd eithafol a allai ddarparu degau o filiynau o arian newydd i mewn i ehangu gwariant ataliol ar atebion ar sail natur. Rydym ar yr adeg honno o'r flwyddyn pan fo pawb yn sôn am y gyllideb, felly wrth i'r sgyrsiau hynny fynd rhagddynt, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i'w gwneud yn flaenoriaeth i ehangu buddsoddiad mewn atebion ar sail natur o fewn eich portffolio?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, not only within my portfolio, as I think there's a huge responsibility across Government on all of us to lean more heavily on nature-based solutions, because we can mix concrete to our heart's content, but, unless we work with the grain of nature, we will always ultimately lose that battle. So, we do have to recalibrate our approach, and we absolutely are committed to those nature-based solutions. The wildfire summit in a few weeks' time will offer, hopefully, the starting gun for some particular work streams around that. I have some particular thoughts around how the sustainable farming scheme and land management can actually support that as well, particularly given the way that farmers stepped up to help fight some of the wildfires that we saw over the summer. Flooding as well, of course—we know there's talk of improving catchment or retaining water through various means in the uplands, et cetera. But key to all of this as well, of course, is it still needs funding, it still needs finance, because the interventions will cost. So, yes, Government has a role to play. Other authorities clearly have a role to play. But nature finance as well, I think, is a key area where we need to be focusing on. I very much intend to build on the work of the previous Government to really focus on that area over the coming months.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, nid yn unig o fewn fy mhortffolio i, gan y credaf fod cyfrifoldeb enfawr ar bob un ohonom ar draws y Llywodraeth i ddibynnu mwy ar atebion ar sail natur, gan y gallwn gymysgu cymaint o goncrit ag y dymunwn, ond oni bai ein bod yn gweithio gyda graen natur, byddwn bob amser yn colli'r frwydr honno yn y pen draw. Felly, rhaid inni ailraddio ein dull o weithredu, ac rydym wedi ymrwymo'n llwyr i atebion ar sail natur. Rwy'n gobeithio y bydd yr uwchgynhadledd ar danau gwyllt ymhen ychydig wythnosau yn cynnig man cychwyn ar gyfer rhai ffrydiau gwaith penodol o amgylch hynny. Mae gennyf rai syniadau penodol ynghylch sut y gall y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy a rheoli tir gefnogi hynny hefyd, yn enwedig o ystyried y ffordd y camodd ffermwyr i'r adwy i helpu i ymladd rhai o'r tanau gwyllt a welsom dros yr haf. Llifogydd hefyd, wrth gwrs—gwyddom fod sôn am wella dalgylchoedd neu gadw dŵr drwy wahanol ddulliau yn yr ucheldiroedd ac yn y blaen. Ond yr hyn sy'n allweddol i hyn oll hefyd wrth gwrs yw bod angen ei ariannu, mae'n dal i fod angen cyllid, gan y bydd yr ymyriadau'n costio. Felly, oes, mae gan y Llywodraeth rôl i'w chwarae. Mae'n amlwg fod gan awdurdodau eraill rôl i'w chwarae. Ond mae cyllid natur hefyd yn faes allweddol y mae angen inni ganolbwyntio arno. Rwy'n bwriadu adeiladu ar waith y Llywodraeth flaenorol i ganolbwyntio'n fanwl ar y maes hwnnw dros y misoedd nesaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cabinet Minister, I'm really encouraged by your answer there, and I look forward to seeing these developments over the coming months. I think there's particular potential within the optional and collaborative layers of the SFS for that as well.

Turning to another matter, a review of the code of practice for the rearing of game birds for sporting purposes in Wales is overdue, with animal welfare organisations such as the League Against Cruel Sports concerned that this is an issue that is being overlooked. This is perhaps borne out by the data. There were no inspections of game bird farms in either 2023 or 2024 and just four since 2025, and those uncovered two breaches of the code of practice. We also have shocking evidence from Animal Aid site visits of three game bird breeding farms in Wales that found conditions falling far below the standards that we all expect. What assessment has the Welsh Government made of the treatment and welfare conditions of game birds bred and reared to be shot for sport, and what plans do you have to ensure that the code is reviewed to ensure it is fit for purpose?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Weinidog Cabinet, rwyf wedi fy nghalonogi'n fawr gan eich ateb yno, ac edrychaf ymlaen at weld y datblygiadau hyn dros y misoedd nesaf. Rwy'n credu bod potensial penodol o fewn haenau dewisol a chydweithredol y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy ar gyfer hynny hefyd.

Gan droi at fater arall, mae'n hen bryd cynnal adolygiad o'r cod ymarfer ar gyfer magu adar hela at ddibenion chwaraeon yng Nghymru, gyda sefydliadau lles anifeiliaid fel y Gynghrair yn Erbyn Chwaraeon Creulon yn pryderu bod hwn yn fater sy'n cael ei anwybyddu. Efallai fod hyn yn cael ei gadarnhau gan y data. Ni chafwyd unrhyw arolygiadau o ffermydd adar hela yn 2023 na 2024, a dim ond pedwar sydd wedi'u cynnal ers 2025, a datgelodd y rheini ddau achos o dorri'r cod ymarfer. Mae gennym dystiolaeth syfrdanol hefyd o ymweliadau safle Animal Aid â thair fferm fridio adar hela yng Nghymru a ganfu fod yr amodau ymhell islaw'r safonau y mae pob un ohonom yn eu disgwyl. Pa asesiad y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o driniaeth ac amodau lles adar hela sy'n cael eu bridio a'u magu i'w saethu at ddibenion chwaraeon, a pha gynlluniau sydd gennych i sicrhau bod y cod yn cael ei adolygu i sicrhau ei fod yn addas i’r diben?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that. I'm not 100 per cent sure where we are on that. I am aware, if I'm correct, and I don't wish to mislead the Senedd, that a review is happening of the evidence at the minute. I'm awaiting advice from officials. Maybe, if you'd allow me, I will write to you to give you an update of where we are, because it is an area that clearly needs to be addressed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Nid wyf 100 y cant yn siŵr ble rydym arni ar hynny. Rwy'n ymwybodol, os wyf yn gywir, ac nid wyf am gamarwain y Senedd, fod adolygiad yn mynd rhagddo o'r dystiolaeth ar hyn o bryd. Rwy'n aros am gyngor gan swyddogion. Os caf, efallai y gallwn ysgrifennu atoch i roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf i chi ynglŷn â ble rydym arni, gan ei bod yn amlwg fod hwn yn faes y mae angen mynd i'r afael ag ef.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You announced at the Royal Welsh Show the national food strategy, which you have got a group working on at the moment, and I commend you for doing that, because it's something that has been missing. But it's really vital that both ends are joined up—the farm gate and the retailer selling to the consumer. Are you confident that you've got the mix right on that group? Because, when I look at the people on there, there doesn't seem to be a major retailer, who, at the end of the day, passes the bulk of the food on to the consumer. And I don't believe you've got a major processor on there either. And those are two key ingredients that are required to build a sustainable chain of supply here in Wales. I hope it'll be successful.

And the other thing that is required is your ability to use legislation to drive improvements in public procurement and nutritional standards. You supported my colleague Peter Fox's Bill when it came to the floor of the Senedd. Will you commit today, as a Minister, that whatever the food strategy group recommends, and if it requires legislation to support those recommendations, you will pilot that through the Senedd as a Government Minister?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn Sioe Frenhinol Cymru, fe gyhoeddoch chi'r strategaeth fwyd genedlaethol, y mae gennych grŵp yn gweithio arni ar hyn o bryd, ac rwy'n eich canmol am wneud hynny, gan ei fod yn rhywbeth sydd wedi bod ar goll. Ond mae'n hanfodol fod y ddau ben yn cysylltu—gât y fferm a'r manwerthwr sy'n gwerthu i'r prynwr. A ydych chi'n hyderus fod y cymysgedd yn gywir gennych yn y grŵp hwnnw? Oherwydd pan edrychaf ar y bobl sy'n aelodau ohono, nid yw'n ymddangos bod yno fanwerthwr mawr, sydd, yn y pen draw, yn darparu'r rhan fwyaf o'r bwyd i'r prynwr. Ac ni chredaf fod gennych brosesydd mawr yno chwaith. A dyna ddau gynhwysyn allweddol sydd eu hangen i adeiladu cadwyn gyflenwi gynaliadwy yma yng Nghymru. Rwy'n gobeithio y bydd yn llwyddiannus.

A'r peth arall sydd ei angen yw eich gallu i ddefnyddio deddfwriaeth i ysgogi gwelliannau ym maes caffael cyhoeddus a safonau maeth. Fe wnaethoch chi gefnogi Bil fy nghyd-Aelod Peter Fox pan gafodd ei drafod yn y Senedd. A wnewch chi ymrwymo heddiw, fel Gweinidog, beth bynnag y mae'r grŵp strategaeth bwyd yn ei argymell, ac os oes angen deddfwriaeth i gefnogi'r argymhellion hynny, y byddwch yn ei llywio drwy'r Senedd fel Gweinidog Llywodraeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. There were a couple of questions in there. I haven't got the list in front of me of the membership of that group, but we are, you're right, looking at a whole food system, from gate to plate and beyond—well, no, where does it go after that? I'm not sure. [Laughter.] But, certainly, there is a need to make sure that all voices are heard around that table. And I know, of course, that the group itself will be utilising work streams that will draw on experience of others also through other fora and networks. And I know that the chair has engaged widely, to say the least, already, beyond what has been brought together around that particular stakeholder group.

It will have a number of work streams. We want to look at areas around the red meat supply chain in Wales. We want to look at horticulture and growing horticulture, and we want to look at food in schools initially. Those are some of the areas that will be prioritised in the first place. So, clearly, if we're looking at the red meat supply chain, then processors and others will be a big, big part of that conversation.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Roedd un neu ddau o gwestiynau yno. Nid oes rhestr o aelodau'r grŵp hwnnw wrth law gennyf, ond rydych chi'n llygad eich lle, rydym yn edrych ar system fwyd gyfan, o'r gât i'r plât a thu hwnt—wel, na, i ble mae'n mynd ar ôl hynny? Nid wyf yn siŵr. [Chwerthin.] Ond yn sicr, mae angen sicrhau bod pob llais yn cael ei glywed o amgylch y bwrdd hwnnw. Ac wrth gwrs, rwy'n gwybod y bydd y grŵp ei hun yn defnyddio ffrydiau gwaith a fydd yn manteisio ar brofiad eraill hefyd drwy fforymau a rhwydweithiau eraill. A gwn fod y cadeirydd eisoes wedi ymgysylltu'n eang, a dweud y lleiaf, y tu hwnt i'r hyn sydd wedi'i ddwyn ynghyd o amgylch y grŵp rhanddeiliaid penodol hwnnw.

Bydd ganddo nifer o ffrydiau gwaith. Rydym am edrych ar feysydd o amgylch y gadwyn gyflenwi cig coch yng Nghymru. Rydym am edrych ar arddwriaeth a thyfu garddwriaeth, ac rydym am edrych ar fwyd mewn ysgolion i gychwyn. Dyna rai o'r meysydd a fydd yn cael eu blaenoriaethu yn y lle cyntaf. Felly, yn amlwg, os ydym yn edrych ar y gadwyn gyflenwi cig coch, bydd proseswyr ac eraill yn rhan fawr iawn o'r sgwrs honno.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I didn't hear you refer to the legislation, and I'd be grateful if you'd reply back to me on that, because, as I said, you did support the food Bill when it first came here. Sadly, the Government at the time rejected it. I think it's an important instrument to use to drive up nutritional standards and also local procurement.

But I'd also like to raise with you the point that I raised with you in committee the other day about the fertiliser tax that's coming in in January of this year. That could potentially be devastating to the ability to procure fertiliser to grow the crops for next year's harvest. And at a time when the uncertainty in the middle east is driving up fertiliser prices to double what they should be at this time of year for forward buying, it seems madness to me to actually introduce a fertiliser tax. Will you now lobby the Westminster Government—the point I made to you in committee—to hold that off for at least 12 months, as the National Farmers Union were asking, so that that situation, hopefully, in the middle east can get back to a sense of normality, so that that price pressure can come out of the system and farmers can purchase the fertiliser they need with confidence that there isn't this supertax being applied to it?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ni chlywais unrhyw gyfeiriad gennych at y ddeddfwriaeth, a buaswn yn ddiolchgar pe baech yn ymateb i mi ar hynny, oherwydd fel y dywedais, fe gefnogoch chi'r Bil bwyd pan ddaeth yma gyntaf. Yn anffodus, fe'i gwrthodwyd gan y Llywodraeth ar y pryd. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn arf pwysig i'w ddefnyddio i godi safonau maeth a chaffael lleol hefyd.

Ond hoffwn godi gyda chi hefyd y pwynt a godais gyda chi yn y pwyllgor y diwrnod o'r blaen ynglŷn â'r dreth ar wrtaith a ddaw i rym ym mis Ionawr. Gallai honno fod yn ddinistriol i'r gallu i gaffael gwrtaith er mwyn tyfu'r cnydau ar gyfer y cynhaeaf y flwyddyn nesaf. Ac ar adeg pan fo'r ansicrwydd yn y dwyrain canol yn codi prisiau gwrtaith i ddwbl yr hyn y dylent fod ar yr adeg hon o'r flwyddyn ar gyfer prynu ymlaen llaw, mae cyflwyno treth ar wrtaith yn swnio'n gwbl wallgof i mi. A wnewch chi lobïo Llywodraeth San Steffan nawr—y pwynt a wneuthum i chi yn y pwyllgor—i ohirio hynny am o leiaf 12 mis, fel roedd Undeb Cenedlaethol yr Amaethwyr yn ei ofyn, fel y gall y sefyllfa yn y dwyrain canol ddychwelyd i ryw fath o normalrwydd, gobeithio, heb bwysau o'r fath ar brisiau yn y system, ac er mwyn i ffermwyr allu prynu'r gwrtaith sydd ei angen arnynt gyda hyder na chaiff y dreth ychwanegol hon ei hychwanegu ato?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, after the session we had in committee, I made sure that I did write to the UK Government to make these representations, to make sure that any implications for Welsh agriculture are properly considered and any negative consequences are avoided. My understanding is, of course, that most of the fertiliser coming to the UK is from the EU—so they wouldn't be affected by the carbon border adjustment mechanism—mainly from the Netherlands, Norway, Germany, and Belgium. But there is some coming from beyond, and we need to guard against any negative consequences stemming from that.

To come back to your previous question as well, if we need to legislate on certain areas, we will. I think we need to wait and see what they recommend. I would prefer action that doesn't require legislation in order to get on with it more quickly, but where we do need to legislate, we won't shy away from that.

And on strengthening procurement policy as well, I know that there will be the publication of a new statement on public procurement policy from this Welsh Government soon, and I'm sure the relevant Minister will publish that when it's ready.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, ar ôl y sesiwn a gawsom yn y pwyllgor, gwneuthum yn siŵr fy mod wedi ysgrifennu at Lywodraeth y DU i wneud y sylwadau hyn, i sicrhau bod unrhyw oblygiadau i amaethyddiaeth Cymru yn cael eu hystyried yn llawn a bod unrhyw ganlyniadau negyddol yn cael eu hosgoi. Fy nealltwriaeth i, wrth gwrs, yw bod y rhan fwyaf o'r gwrtaith a ddaw i'r DU yn dod o'r UE—felly ni fyddent yn cael eu heffeithio gan y mecanwaith addasu pris carbon ar draws ffiniau—yn bennaf o'r Iseldiroedd, Norwy, yr Almaen, a Gwlad Belg. Ond mae rhywfaint yn dod o fannau pellach, ac mae angen inni warchod rhag unrhyw ganlyniadau negyddol sy'n deillio o hynny.

I ddod yn ôl at eich cwestiwn blaenorol hefyd, os oes angen inni ddeddfu ar rai meysydd, byddwn yn gwneud hynny. Rwy'n credu bod angen inni aros i weld beth y maent yn ei argymell. Buasai'n well gennyf weld gweithredu nad oes angen deddfwriaeth ar ei gyfer er mwyn gallu bwrw ymlaen yn gyflymach, ond lle mae angen inni ddeddfu, ni fyddwn yn osgoi gwneud hynny.

Ac o ran cryfhau polisi caffael hefyd, gwn y bydd datganiad newydd ar bolisi caffael cyhoeddus yn cael ei wneud gan y Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru cyn bo hir, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd y Gweinidog perthnasol yn ei gyhoeddi pan fydd yn barod.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Groundwater Sources

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod ffynonellau dŵr daear, y gallai datblygiadau mawr effeithio arnynt, yn cael eu diogelu a'u monitro'n briodol? OQ64604
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What action is the Welsh Government taking to ensure that groundwater sources that could be affected by major developments are appropriately protected and monitored? OQ64604

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Protecting groundwater is essential for safeguarding drinking water supplies, the environment and Wales's long-term water resilience. Planning and environmental permitting processes require risks to groundwater to be assessed and managed. Where risks are identified, Natural Resources Wales can then require mitigation measures, monitoring and ongoing controls to protect water resources.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae diogelu dŵr daear yn hanfodol ar gyfer diogelu cyflenwadau dŵr yfed, yr amgylchedd a gwydnwch dŵr hirdymor Cymru. Mae prosesau cynllunio a thrwyddedu amgylcheddol yn ei gwneud yn ofynnol i asesu a rheoli risgiau dŵr daear. Lle nodir risgiau, gall Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru fynnu mesurau lliniaru, monitro a rheolaethau parhaus i ddiogelu adnoddau dŵr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Access to clean and safe groundwater is essential for protecting public health, supporting agriculture and safeguarding our natural environment. As major developments come forward across Wales, it is vital that local communities can feel confident that groundwater sources are being properly monitored and protected. Can you outline how the Welsh Government is working with Natural Resources Wales and the local planning authorities to ensure that groundwater resources are robustly monitored, protected and transparently assessed before major developments are approved?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae mynediad at ddŵr daear glân a diogel yn hanfodol ar gyfer diogelu iechyd y cyhoedd, cefnogi amaethyddiaeth a diogelu ein hamgylchedd naturiol. Wrth i ddatblygiadau mawr ddigwydd ledled Cymru, mae'n hanfodol y gall cymunedau lleol deimlo'n hyderus fod ffynonellau dŵr daear yn cael eu monitro a'u diogelu'n briodol. A allwch chi amlinellu sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n gweithio gyda Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru a'r awdurdodau cynllunio lleol i sicrhau bod adnoddau dŵr daear yn cael eu monitro'n gadarn, eu diogelu a'u hasesu'n dryloyw cyn cymeradwyo datblygiadau mawr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that question. I know that this is a challenge that could occur in a number of different contexts. I hope you'll be reassured that the Welsh Government is working with Natural Resources Wales and local planning authorities through the planning and environmental permitting systems to make sure that groundwater risks are identified and that they are properly assessed and managed before major developments proceed.

We set the national planning policy framework that local planning authorities apply when determining applications, and Natural Resources Wales provide specialist technical advice on groundwater risks as a statutory consultee. Planning authorities can draw on their hydrogeological expertise when they consider whether further investigation or any mitigation or monitoring is needed before a decision is taken. 

Where evidence identifies a specific local risk, local planning authorities and NRW can use their respective planning and permitting functions to make sure that proportionate monitoring and controls are in place during construction and operation. But, ultimately, we will work closely with those bodies to support the consistent and effective application of groundwater protections as a number of different development pressures—and environmental risks, no doubt—evolve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am eich cwestiwn. Gwn fod hon yn her a allai godi mewn nifer o gyd-destunau gwahanol. Rwy'n gobeithio y cewch chi eich sicrhau bod Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ac awdurdodau cynllunio lleol drwy'r systemau cynllunio a thrwyddedu amgylcheddol i wneud yn siŵr bod risgiau dŵr daear yn cael eu nodi a'u bod yn cael eu hasesu a'u rheoli'n briodol cyn i unrhyw ddatblygiadau mawr fynd rhagddynt.

Ni sy'n gosod y fframwaith polisi cynllunio cenedlaethol y mae awdurdodau cynllunio lleol yn ei ddefnyddio wrth benderfynu ar geisiadau, ac mae Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn darparu cyngor technegol arbenigol ar risgiau dŵr daear fel ymgynghorai statudol. Gall awdurdodau cynllunio ddefnyddio eu harbenigedd hydroddaearegol pan fyddant yn ystyried a oes angen ymchwilio ymhellach neu unrhyw liniaru neu fonitro cyn gwneud penderfyniad.

Lle mae tystiolaeth yn nodi risg leol benodol, gall awdurdodau cynllunio lleol a Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ddefnyddio eu swyddogaethau cynllunio a thrwyddedu priodol i sicrhau bod trefniadau monitro a rheolaethau cymesur ar waith yn y cyfnod adeiladu a'r cyfnod gweithredol. Ond yn y pen draw, byddwn yn gweithio'n agos gyda'r cyrff hynny i gefnogi'r gwaith o roi amddiffyniadau dŵr daear ar waith yn gyson ac yn effeithiol wrth i nifer o wahanol bwysau datblygu—a risgiau amgylcheddol, heb os—esblygu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This links back to the Member's question, but I want to go a bit more local. The Welsh Water treatment works in Gowerton serves around 58,000 constituents across Gŵyr Abertawe. However, concerns have been raised that proposed housing developments in Gowerton and surrounding areas could place unsustainable pressure on waste water networks and storage capacity.

Natural Resources Wales has already suspended major developments due to rising nitrate levels in the Loughor estuary. Also, local residents, through Save Gowerton from Gridlock, have warned that the proposed 216-home development would exacerbate traffic congestion on Victoria Road. 

What action is the Welsh Government taking to address the concerns identified by NRW and Welsh Water, and to ensure that essential infrastructure in Gowerton is not overwhelmed and that further damage is not caused to our waterways?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae hyn yn cysylltu â chwestiwn yr Aelod, ond rwyf am fynd ychydig yn fwy lleol. Mae gwaith trin Dŵr Cymru yn Nhre-gŵyr yn gwasanaethu oddeutu 58,000 o etholwyr ledled Gŵyr Abertawe. Fodd bynnag, mae pryderon wedi'u codi y gallai datblygiadau tai arfaethedig yn Nhre-gŵyr a'r ardaloedd cyfagos roi pwysau anghynaliadwy ar rwydweithiau dŵr gwastraff a chapasiti storio.

Mae Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru eisoes wedi atal datblygiadau mawr dros dro oherwydd lefelau nitradau cynyddol yn aber afon Llwchwr. Hefyd, mae trigolion lleol, drwy grŵp Save Gowerton from Gridlock, wedi rhybuddio y byddai'r datblygiad arfaethedig o 216 o gartrefi yn gwaethygu tagfeydd traffig ar Heol Victoria.

Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â'r pryderon a nodwyd gan CNC a Dŵr Cymru, ac i sicrhau nad yw seilwaith hanfodol yn Nhre-gŵyr yn cael ei orlethu ac nad oes rhagor o ddifrod yn cael ei achosi i'n dyfrffyrdd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing attention to a very important area here. I won't get drawn on particular local issues, but, more generally, we do know that the nutrient impact on housing delivery is concerning. The Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning and I both recognise the importance of this issue. 

To strengthen leadership and strategic co-ordination to try and address those nutrient-related challenges, the Welsh Government is establishing a new nutrient efficiency and resilience group. That group will bring together key partners and stakeholders, including regulators, water companies, the agricultural sector, environmental organisations and local authority representatives, to provide strategic oversight of nutrient management across Wales.

Its work will focus on both the immediate operational challenges, which are pressing, but also the longer term actions needed to restore and improve the health of our rivers and catchments, helping to deliver a more co-ordinated and whole-system approach to river recovery and environmental improvement, but also, hopefully, unlocking potential developments such as the one that you've referred to.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am dynnu sylw at faes pwysig iawn yma. Nid wyf am drafod materion lleol penodol, ond yn fwy cyffredinol, gwyddom fod effaith maethynnau ar y cyflenwad tai yn peri pryder. Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio a minnau'n cydnabod pwysigrwydd y mater hwn.

Er mwyn cryfhau arweinyddiaeth a chydgysylltu strategol i geisio mynd i'r afael â'r heriau sy'n gysylltiedig â maethynnau, mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n sefydlu grŵp newydd ar effeithlonrwydd a gwydnwch maethynnau. Bydd y grŵp hwnnw'n dwyn partneriaid a rhanddeiliaid allweddol ynghyd, gan gynnwys rheoleiddwyr, cwmnïau dŵr, y sector amaethyddol, sefydliadau amgylcheddol a chynrychiolwyr awdurdodau lleol, i ddarparu goruchwyliaeth strategol ar reolaeth maethynnau ledled Cymru.

Bydd ei waith yn canolbwyntio ar yr heriau gweithredol uniongyrchol, sy'n heriau dybryd, ond hefyd ar y camau gweithredu mwy hirdymor sydd eu hangen i adfer a gwella iechyd ein hafonydd a'n dalgylchoedd, gan helpu i gyflawni dull mwy cydgysylltiedig a system gyfan o adfer afonydd a gwella'r amgylchedd, ond hefyd, gobeithio, i ddatgloi datblygiadau posibl fel yr un y cyfeirioch chi ato.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Family Farms

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddiogelu ffermydd teuluol ym Mrycheiniog Tawe Nedd rhag y pwysau ariannol ac amgylcheddol cynyddol sy'n wynebu amaethyddiaeth? OQ64577
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What action is the Welsh Government taking to protect family farms in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd from the growing financial and environmental pressures facing agriculture? OQ64577

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government is supporting family farms in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd through its £340 million annual budget commitment. To help farmers facing significant pressures this year particularly, we've increased advance payments from 70 per cent to 80 per cent. The sustainable farming scheme is an accessible whole-farm scheme, designed to support the long-term resilience of farms.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n cefnogi ffermydd teuluol ym Mrycheiniog Tawe Nedd drwy ei hymrwymiad cyllidebol blynyddol o £340 miliwn. Er mwyn helpu ffermwyr sy'n wynebu pwysau sylweddol eleni yn arbennig, rydym wedi cynyddu'r rhagdaliadau o 70 y cant i 80 y cant. Mae'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn gynllun fferm gyfan hygyrch, sydd wedi'i gynllunio i gefnogi gwydnwch hirdymor ffermydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. Resilience means very little if our family farms cannot survive. Farmers across Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd have endured an incredibly difficult year, as I'm sure you're fully aware, through droughts, wildfires, rising costs and the continued threat of bovine TB, whilst also being expected to adapt to the new sustainable farming scheme. These aren't simply businesses; they produce our food, manage our countryside, support thousands of jobs and keep our rural communities alive. Yet too often farmers tell me they feel these policies have been done to them, rather than being developed with them. Will you guarantee that food production and the survival of the Welsh family farm will be at the heart of your decisions? And also, will you ensure that environmental ambitions work alongside productive farming rather than adding further costs and regulation to the very people we depend upon to feed us and look after our countryside?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Ychydig iawn y mae gwydnwch yn ei olygu os na all ein ffermydd teuluol oroesi. Mae ffermwyr ledled Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd wedi dioddef blwyddyn anodd iawn, fel y gwyddoch rwy'n siŵr, oherwydd sychderau, tanau gwyllt, costau cynyddol a bygythiad parhaus TB buchol, tra bo disgwyl iddynt hefyd addasu i'r cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy newydd. Nid busnesau'n unig yw'r rhain; maent yn cynhyrchu ein bwyd, yn rheoli ein cefn gwlad, yn cefnogi miloedd o swyddi ac yn cadw ein cymunedau gwledig yn fyw. Ac eto, yn rhy aml, dywed ffermwyr wrthyf eu bod yn teimlo bod y polisïau hyn wedi'u gwneud iddynt, yn hytrach na'u bod wedi'u datblygu gyda nhw. A wnewch chi warantu y bydd cynhyrchiant bwyd a goroesiad y fferm deuluol Gymreig yn cael lle canolog yn eich penderfyniadau? Ac a wnewch chi sicrhau hefyd fod uchelgeisiau amgylcheddol yn gweithio ochr yn ochr â ffermio cynhyrchiol yn hytrach nag ychwanegu costau a rheoleiddio pellach i'r union bobl rydym yn dibynnu arnynt i'n bwydo a gofalu am ein cefn gwlad?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes I will, because family farms, as you say, are the backbone of our rural communities in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd and the rest of Wales as well, and we recognise the significant pressures that those businesses are facing. That's why we have been flexible, for example around the control of agricultural pollution regulations, in allowing a longer period to clear some of the slurry stores that farms have, but to do so in a responsible way, in a managed way, in a controlled way. Natural Resources Wales support that approach, because they recognise that there would be additional environmental risks from those stores overspilling or failing, which would be even more catastrophic. So, I'd like to think that we are being pragmatic and practical where we can be.

I spent the summer visiting a number of agricultural shows, and there were three things, basically, that farmers were asking for. One is certainty in a hugely uncertain world, and we are trying to deliver that with our commitment to long-term funding for farming. But they also ask for flexibility. When circumstances change, such as the drought we saw over the summer, then maybe we need to look at the way we ask farms to do things. We've introduced derogations within the SFS in terms of some of the things that they have to achieve directly as a consequence of some of those extreme weather events. The third element was general support. If you look at the red tape review, one of the steps that we've taken, then hopefully we're demonstrating that as well. So yes, we do need to make sure that farming is resilient and is sustainable for the future, and I will do everything I can to achieve that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gwnaf, gan mai ffermydd teuluol, fel y dywedwch, yw asgwrn cefn ein cymunedau gwledig ym Mrycheiniog Tawe Nedd a gweddill Cymru hefyd, ac rydym yn cydnabod y pwysau sylweddol y mae'r busnesau hynny'n ei wynebu. Dyna pam ein bod wedi bod yn hyblyg, o ran rheoli rheoliadau llygredd amaethyddol er enghraifft, drwy ganiatáu cyfnod hirach i glirio rhai o'r storfeydd slyri sydd gan ffermydd, ond i wneud hynny mewn ffordd gyfrifol, mewn ffordd reoledig, o dan reolaeth. Mae Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn cefnogi'r dull hwnnw o weithredu, gan eu bod yn cydnabod y byddai risgiau amgylcheddol ychwanegol pe bai'r storfeydd hynny'n gorlifo neu'n methu, a fyddai hyd yn oed yn fwy trychinebus. Felly, hoffwn feddwl ein bod yn bod yn bragmatig ac yn ymarferol lle gallwn.

Treuliais yr haf yn ymweld â nifer o sioeau amaethyddol, ac roedd tri pheth, yn y bôn, roedd y ffermwyr yn gofyn amdanynt. Un yw sicrwydd mewn byd hynod o ansicr, ac rydym yn ceisio sicrhau hynny gyda'n hymrwymiad i gyllid hirdymor ar gyfer ffermio. Ond maent hefyd yn gofyn am hyblygrwydd. Pan fydd amgylchiadau'n newid, fel y sychder a welsom dros yr haf, efallai fod angen inni edrych ar y ffordd y gofynnwn i ffermydd wneud pethau. Rydym wedi cyflwyno rhanddirymiadau o fewn y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy ar gyfer rhai o'r pethau y mae'n rhaid iddynt eu cyflawni'n uniongyrchol o ganlyniad i rai o'r digwyddiadau tywydd eithafol hynny. Y drydedd elfen oedd cymorth cyffredinol. Os edrychwch ar yr adolygiad o fiwrocratiaeth, sef un o'r camau rydym wedi'u cymryd, rwy'n gobeithio ein bod yn dangos hynny hefyd. Felly oes, mae angen inni sicrhau bod ffermio yn wydn ac yn gynaliadwy ar gyfer y dyfodol, a byddaf yn gwneud popeth yn fy ngallu i gyflawni hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know that many Members were at the NFU reception last week, and hearing the union and farmers thank the Minister for a number of decisions this Welsh Government has taken so far to support them speaks volumes. For the first time, farmers feel heard. Plaid Cymru's manifesto commits to rural-proofing our communities, including those in my constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd. Could we have some information on the progress of the rural development strategy for Wales and how this will tackle poverty and create new economic and social opportunities for my constituents?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwn fod llawer o'r Aelodau yn nerbyniad Undeb Cenedlaethol yr Amaethwyr yr wythnos diwethaf, ac mae clywed yr undeb a'r ffermwyr yn diolch i'r Gweinidog am nifer o benderfyniadau y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru wedi'u gwneud hyd yn hyn i'w cefnogi yn adrodd cyfrolau. Am y tro cyntaf, mae ffermwyr yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu clywed. Mae maniffesto Plaid Cymru yn ymrwymo i sicrhau bod ein polisïau'n addas ar gyfer ein cymunedau gwledig, gan gynnwys y rheini yn fy etholaeth i, sef Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd. A gawn ni rywfaint o wybodaeth am gynnydd strategaeth datblygu gwledig Cymru a sut y bydd yn helpu i drechu tlodi ac yn creu cyfleoedd economaidd a chymdeithasol newydd i fy etholwyr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you very much for the question. I think it's very appropriate that the enterprise Minister is sat next to me, because I fully hope that this will be a joint endeavour. But we are looking to increase that particular focus on some of the communities that feel maybe that they have been marginalised in some of these discussions in the past. But certainly, we want to consider that statutory duty to make sure that, when it comes to creating policy or making funding decisions, for example, that balance and that consideration in the round is taken. It isn't about setting one part of Wales against another. It's making sure that every part of Wales has a fair hearing, and that's certainly, when it comes to the rural-proofing duty, something that we want to achieve. You will be aware that we are consulting at the minute, that there is an opportunity for people to feed in around those proposals, and I very much look forward to receiving those.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr iawn am eich cwestiwn. Rwy'n credu ei bod yn briodol iawn fod y Gweinidog dros fenter yn eistedd wrth fy ymyl, gan y gobeithiaf yn fawr y bydd hon yn ymdrech ar y cyd. Ond rydym yn gobeithio cynyddu'r ffocws penodol hwnnw ar rai o'r cymunedau sy'n teimlo efallai eu bod wedi'u hymyleiddio yn rhai o'r trafodaethau hyn yn y gorffennol. Ond yn sicr, rydym am ystyried y ddyletswydd statudol i sicrhau, wrth greu polisi neu wneud penderfyniadau cyllido er enghraifft, y ceir y cydbwysedd hwnnw a'r ystyriaeth gyffredinol honno. Nid oes a wnelo hyn â gosod un rhan o Gymru yn erbyn y llall. Mae'n sicrhau bod pob rhan o Gymru'n cael gwrandawiad teg, ac mae hynny'n sicr, o ran y ddyletswydd prawfesur gwledig, yn rhywbeth rydym eisiau ei gyflawni. Fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol ein bod yn ymgynghori ar hyn o bryd, fod cyfle i bobl roi eu safbwyntiau ar y cynigion hynny, ac edrychaf ymlaen yn fawr at eu cael.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nature and Biodiversity Targets

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad ar y cynnydd tuag at gyrraedd targedau natur a bioamrywiaeth Llywodraeth Cymru? OQ64581
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on progress towards reaching the Welsh Government's nature and biodiversity targets? OQ64581

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are making good progress in developing ambitious, legally binding biodiversity targets, which we must have in place by April 2028. The targets will be informed by expert and stakeholder advice, underpinned by robust evidence and impact assessment, and supported by delivery of our climate and nature action plan.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym yn gwneud cynnydd da ar ddatblygu targedau bioamrywiaeth uchelgeisiol cyfreithiol rwymol y mae'n rhaid i ni eu rhoi ar waith erbyn mis Ebrill 2028. Bydd y targedau'n cael eu llywio gan gyngor gan arbenigwyr a rhanddeiliaid, wedi'i ategu gan dystiolaeth gadarn ac asesiad effaith, a'i gefnogi gan ein cynllun gweithredu ar yr hinsawdd a natur.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. On 2 June, when I raised this in the Siambr, the First Minister said that the Government is committed to clear public reporting on Wales's progress towards net zero through an accessible online dashboard. I went to have a look for it when some of the other dashboards came out, and all I could find was an old PowerPoint presentation about public sector emissions. Maybe I'm looking in the wrong place. Progress and opportunity for climate resilience is inextricably linked with the need to halt and reverse the loss of nature. I'm glad to see this recognised with the announcement of the forthcoming climate and nature plan, but we need to be clear about how progress on both will be monitored and reported. You'll be aware of the importance of the forthcoming targets due to be introduced in accordance with the Environment (Principles, Governance and Biodiversity Targets) (Wales) Act 2026, yet presently we don't have targets or any clear means of Member oversight on progress. Could you confirm the timeline for the introduction of those biodiversity and nature targets and whether you intend to monitor and report on progress openly using one of those dashboards?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Ar 2 Mehefin, pan godais hyn yn y Siambr, dywedodd y Prif Weinidog fod y Llywodraeth wedi ymrwymo i adrodd cyhoeddus clir ar gynnydd Cymru tuag at sero net drwy ddangosfwrdd ar-lein hygyrch. Euthum i edrych amdano pan gyhoeddwyd rhai o'r dangosfyrddau eraill, a'r cyfan y gallwn ddod o hyd iddo oedd hen gyflwyniad PowerPoint ar allyriadau'r sector cyhoeddus. Efallai fy mod yn chwilio yn y lle anghywir. Mae cysylltiad annatod rhwng cynnydd a chyfle ar gyfer gwrthsefyll newid hinsawdd a'r angen i atal a gwrthdroi colli natur. Rwy'n falch o weld hyn yn cael ei gydnabod gyda chyhoeddi'r cynllun hinsawdd a natur sydd ar y ffordd, ond mae angen inni fod yn glir ynglŷn â sut y bydd cynnydd ar y ddau beth yn cael ei fonitro a'i adrodd. Fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol o bwysigrwydd y targedau sydd ar y ffordd sydd i'w cyflwyno yn unol â Deddf yr Amgylchedd (Egwyddorion, Llywodraethiant a Thargedau Bioamrywiaeth) (Cymru) 2026, ond ar hyn o bryd, nid oes gennym dargedau nac unrhyw ddulliau clir i Aelodau oruchwylio'r cynnydd. A allech chi gadarnhau'r amserlen ar gyfer cyflwyno'r targedau bioamrywiaeth a natur hynny, ac a ydych chi'n bwriadu monitro ac adrodd ar gynnydd yn agored gan ddefnyddio un o'r dangosfyrddau hynny?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question. I am committed, as I said, to setting those targets across all the priority areas, and that work has to be done, in law, by April 2028. So, we will do that. As I said, we will work with stakeholders to get that in place. An independent advisory panel is providing expert scrutiny and evidence-based advice to us, while the biodiversity targets task and finish group brings together stakeholders from key sectors to help make sure that those targets are ambitious but also practical and realistically deliverable. They are being developed within a complex social, economic and environmental system. I could bore you with the theory of change and cost-benefit analysis and all of the work that's happening, but they are critical tools to understand that pathway to delivery, to assess the likely impacts and benefits of different interventions and then to build that robust evidence base that we need to support targeted development, implementation and evaluation. I hear what the Member is saying about transparency. I would expect that we would be looking to do that. I will maybe ask my colleague the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution to write to you with an outline. But, certainly, we intend to do that with other metrics across Government, and I can't imagine that it would not be the case here as well.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn. Rwyf wedi ymrwymo, fel y dywedais, i osod y targedau hynny ar draws yr holl feysydd blaenoriaeth, ac mae'n rhaid gwneud y gwaith hwnnw, yn ôl y gyfraith, erbyn mis Ebrill 2028. Felly, byddwn yn gwneud hynny. Fel y dywedais, byddwn yn gweithio gyda rhanddeiliaid i roi hynny ar waith. Mae panel cynghori annibynnol yn gwneud gwaith craffu arbenigol ac yn darparu cyngor sy'n seiliedig ar dystiolaeth i ni, tra bo'r grŵp gorchwyl a gorffen ar dargedau bioamrywiaeth yn dwyn rhanddeiliaid ynghyd o sectorau allweddol i helpu i sicrhau bod y targedau hynny'n uchelgeisiol ond hefyd yn ymarferol ac y gellir eu cyflawni'n realistig. Maent yn cael eu datblygu o fewn system gymdeithasol, economaidd ac amgylcheddol gymhleth. Gallwn eich diflasu â'r theori newid a'r dadansoddiad cost a budd a'r holl waith sy'n mynd rhagddo, ond maent yn arfau hanfodol i ddeall y llwybr tuag at gyflawniad, i asesu effeithiau a manteision tebygol gwahanol ymyriadau ac yna i adeiladu'r sylfaen dystiolaeth gadarn sydd ei hangen arnom i gefnogi gweithredu, gwerthuso a datblygu wedi'i dargedu. Rwy'n clywed yr hyn y mae'r Aelod yn ei ddweud ynglŷn â thryloywder. Buaswn yn disgwyl i ni geisio gwneud hynny. Efallai y byddaf yn gofyn i fy nghyd-Aelod, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a’r Cyfansoddiad, ysgrifennu atoch gydag amlinelliad. Ond yn sicr, rydym yn bwriadu gwneud hynny gyda metrigau eraill ar draws y Llywodraeth, ac ni allaf ddychmygu na fyddai'n wir yma hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Last week, I asked the First Minister about the fact that NRW and other agencies do not know the full mix of chemicals discharged legally into the rivers of Carmarthenshire. A report has said that NRW are flying blind. As I wasn't quite sure of the response from the Cabinet Minister, I will ask the Cabinet Minister this: if we do not know exactly what chemicals are discharged into the rivers and how they interact with each other, how can we know what impact they are having on river ecosystems? How can we say with any confidence that this cocktail of pollutants isn't disrupting fish migration, harming fish and aquatic plants, and irreparably affecting river diversity? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yr wythnos diwethaf, gofynnais i'r Prif Weinidog ynglŷn â'r ffaith nad yw Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ac asiantaethau eraill yn gwybod beth yw'r cymysgedd llawn o gemegau sy'n cael eu gollwng yn gyfreithlon i afonydd sir Gaerfyrddin. Mae adroddiad wedi dweud bod Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn hedfan yn ddall. Gan nad oeddwn yn gwbl sicr o ymateb y Gweinidog Cabinet, fe ofynnaf hyn i'r Gweinidog Cabinet: os nad ydym yn gwybod yn union pa gemegau sy'n cael eu gollwng i'r afonydd a sut y maent yn rhyngweithio â'i gilydd, sut y gallwn wybod pa effaith y maent yn ei chael ar ecosystemau afonydd? Sut y gallwn ddweud gydag unrhyw hyder nad yw'r cymysgedd hwn o lygryddion yn tarfu ar batrymau mudo pysgod, yn niweidio pysgod a phlanhigion dyfrol, ac yn cael effaith anadferadwy ar amrywiaeth afonydd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I meet regularly with Natural Resources Wales. This is something that I will raise with them. Clearly, I have confidence in their ability to do their job, but I also recognise that they are being stretched and there is great demand on the expertise that they have. But I will pursue that with them and ask for an explanation.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rwy'n cyfarfod yn rheolaidd â Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth y byddaf yn ei godi gyda nhw. Yn amlwg, mae gennyf hyder yn eu gallu i wneud eu gwaith, ond rwyf hefyd yn cydnabod eu bod o dan bwysau a bod galw mawr am yr arbenigedd sydd ganddynt. Ond fe af ar drywydd hyn gyda nhw a gofyn iddynt am esboniad.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I welcome your rapid first steps on the climate and nature action plan for Wales, because if we're going to meet net zero by 2040 and achieve substantial nature recovery by 2050, we'll need to keep moving quickly and effectively, because the pace at which nature is declining in recent years is truly alarming. Since before the election, I've been in touch with groups like Save the River Usk, who are not just bringing much-needed attention to the subject but also building up detailed data sets at a grass-roots level, providing crucial local insights about the impact of the climate and nature crisis. You've said that the Government's new climate and nature board will reflect the experiences and priorities of people and communities across Wales. Will there be a role for informed and organised groups, like Save the River Usk, on the board so that their local knowledge and experience can be harnessed? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu eich camau cyntaf cyflym ar gynllun gweithredu hinsawdd a natur Cymru, oherwydd os ydym am gyrraedd sero net erbyn 2040 a chyflawni adferiad natur sylweddol erbyn 2050, bydd angen inni barhau i symud yn gyflym ac yn effeithiol, gan ei bod yn wirioneddol frawychus pa mor gyflym y mae natur wedi dirywio yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf. Ers cyn yr etholiad, rwyf wedi bod mewn cysylltiad â grwpiau fel Achub Afon Wysg, sydd nid yn unig yn dod â sylw mawr ei angen i'r pwnc, ond hefyd yn adeiladu setiau data manwl ar lefel llawr gwlad, gan ddarparu mewnwelediad lleol hanfodol ynglŷn ag effaith yr argyfwng hinsawdd a natur. Rydych chi wedi dweud y bydd bwrdd hinsawdd a natur newydd y Llywodraeth yn adlewyrchu profiadau a blaenoriaethau pobl a chymunedau ledled Cymru. A fydd rôl i grwpiau gwybodus a threfnus, fel Achub Afon Wysg, ar y bwrdd fel y gellir manteisio ar eu gwybodaeth a'u profiad lleol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I will happily take that away and consider it. I think you make a fair point. I think the role of citizens—. And I said earlier, in relation to green spaces, when you empower citizens to take action and to respond to some of these circumstances, then you are really creating a more sustainable approach, moving forward. Citizen science, as well, I think, has a role to play. So, we'll consider all of that in the mix, and it's certainly something I can take on board. It's a point very well made.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n fwy na pharod i ystyried hynny. Rwy'n credu eich bod yn gwneud pwynt teg. Rwy'n credu bod rôl dinasyddion—. A dywedais yn gynharach, mewn perthynas â mannau gwyrdd, pan fyddwch chi'n grymuso dinasyddion i weithredu ac ymateb i rai o'r amgylchiadau hyn, rydych chi'n creu dull o weithredu mwy cynaliadwy, wrth symud ymlaen. Rwy'n credu bod gan wyddoniaeth dinasyddion rôl i'w chwarae hefyd. Felly, byddwn yn ystyried hyn oll yn rhan o'r cymysgedd, ac mae'n sicr yn rhywbeth y gallaf ei ystyried. Mae'n bwynt da iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Sustainability of Livestock Numbers

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa asesiad mae'r Llywodraeth wedi'i wneud o gynaliadwyedd niferoedd da byw yng Nghymru? OQ64573
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What assessment has the Government made of the sustainability of livestock numbers in Wales? OQ64573

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, the Government monitors livestock numbers alongside evidence on farm viability, on emissions, on biodiversity and on animal health, including through the UK Agriculture Market Monitoring Group. Our aim, of course, is to support sustainable, productive farming, and the sustainable farming scheme, for example, will help farmers improve resilience, strengthen food production and, of course, environmental outcomes at the same time.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, mae'r Llywodraeth yn monitro niferoedd da byw ochr yn ochr â thystiolaeth ar hyfywedd ffermydd, ar allyriadau, ar fioamrywiaeth ac ar iechyd anifeiliaid, gan gynnwys drwy Grŵp Monitro Marchnad Amaethyddol y DU. Ein nod, wrth gwrs, yw cefnogi ffermio cynaliadwy, cynhyrchiol, a bydd y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy, er enghraifft, yn helpu ffermwyr i wella gwydnwch, cryfhau cynhyrchiant bwyd, a chanlyniadau amgylcheddol ar yr un pryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. My colleague Laura Anne Jones mentioned back in July that Westminster's Climate Change Committee recommended a 25 per cent reduction in livestock numbers by 2040 in order to hit net-zero targets. Now, you've stated that there are no plans for a reduction, and that is something that I welcome, but it raises a further question to me, and it's one that's been discussed in this Chamber today. Given your dual role as Minister for rural resilience and sustainability, in scenarios where the interests of our rural communities stand in direct contrast with actions necessitated by net-zero policy, will you choose to back our farmers or bow to the interests of the climate lobby?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Soniodd fy nghyd-Aelod Laura Anne Jones yn ôl ym mis Gorffennaf fod Pwyllgor Newid Hinsawdd San Steffan wedi argymell gostyngiad o 25 y cant yn niferoedd da byw erbyn 2040 er mwyn cyrraedd targedau sero net. Nawr, rydych chi wedi datgan nad oes unrhyw gynlluniau ar gyfer gostyngiad, ac mae hynny'n rhywbeth rwy'n ei groesawu, ond mae'n codi cwestiwn pellach i mi, ac mae'n un sydd wedi'i drafod yn y Siambr hon heddiw. O ystyried eich rôl ddeuol fel Gweinidog gwydnwch a chynaliadwyedd gwledig, mewn senarios lle mae buddiannau ein cymunedau gwledig yn gwrthgyferbynnu'n uniongyrchol â chamau gweithredu sy'n ofynnol yn sgil y polisi sero net, a fyddwch chi'n dewis cefnogi ein ffermwyr neu'n plygu i fuddiannau'r lobi hinsawdd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think this is where Reform gets it wrong. You see it as one side against another. I would much rather find a way where we can mutually support both farming, by making it more resilient, but, in doing so, support the recovery of nature and tackling climate change as well. It isn't an either/or. I believe that we can—. And look, farming needs to become resilient. Nobody knows more than farmers the impact of climate change. They are the ones who are in the face of drought over the summer. They are the ones whose land sits under floodwaters for weeks on end. That has a direct impact on the economic bottom line. Many of the farmers I work with are the first ones to say, ‘We need to stop this flooding happening. We need support from Government and others to develop some of these interventions. Not only will it help nature and the environment, but, by damn, it will make our business more sustainable moving forward.' So, that is my approach, not this 'let's go and look for a fight' approach that we get from Reform.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu mai dyma lle mae Reform yn camgymryd. Rydych chi'n ei weld fel un ochr yn erbyn y llall. Byddai'n llawer gwell gennyf i ddod o hyd i ffordd o gefnogi'r ddau, amaethyddiaeth, drwy ei gwneud yn fwy gwydn, ond wrth wneud hynny, cefnogi adfer natur a mynd i'r afael â newid hinsawdd hefyd. Nid yw'n ddewis rhwng y naill neu'r llall. Rwy'n credu y gallwn ni—. Ac edrychwch, mae angen i amaethyddiaeth fod yn wydn. Mae ffermwyr yn gwybod yn well na neb am effaith newid hinsawdd. Nhw sy'n wynebu sychder yn ystod yr haf. Nhw sy'n gweld eu tir o dan ddŵr llifogydd am wythnosau bwy'i gilydd. Mae hynny'n cael effaith uniongyrchol ar y sylfaen economaidd. Mae llawer o'r ffermwyr rwy'n gweithio gyda nhw gyda'r cyntaf i ddweud, 'Mae angen inni atal y llifogydd hyn rhag digwydd. Mae angen cefnogaeth gan y Llywodraeth ac eraill arnom i ddatblygu rhai o'r ymyriadau hyn. Nid yn unig y bydd yn helpu natur a'r amgylchedd, fe fydd hefyd yn gwneud ein busnes yn fwy cynaliadwy wrth symud ymlaen.' Felly, dyna fy agwedd i, nid yr agwedd 'beth am fynd i chwilio am ffrae' a gawn gan Reform.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rural Resilience

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. How is the Welsh Government promoting rural resilience in Casnewydd Islwyn? OQ64590

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, we are, I can assure the Member. We are strengthening rural resilience, Dirprwy Lywydd, across all rural Wales through investment in sustainable farming, in support for rural communities and businesses, actions to improve climate resilience, and new proposals for our rural-proofing duty, to make sure that the needs of rural areas are considered, of course, when developing policy programmes and spending plans as well.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, gallaf sicrhau'r Aelod ein bod yn gwneud hynny. Rydym yn cryfhau gwydnwch gwledig, Ddirprwy Lywydd, ar draws y Gymru wledig yn ei chyfanrwydd drwy fuddsoddi mewn ffermio cynaliadwy, drwy gefnogaeth i gymunedau a busnesau gwledig, gweithredoedd i wella gwydnwch hinsawdd, a chynigion newydd ar gyfer ein dyletswydd prawfesur gwledig, i sicrhau bod anghenion ardaloedd gwledig yn cael eu hystyried, wrth gwrs, wrth ddatblygu rhaglenni polisi a chynlluniau gwariant hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am yr ateb yna, a dwi'n falch eich bod chi yn gwneud yr holl waith yna hefyd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that response, and I'm pleased that you are doing all of that work.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I want to turn to a specific issue that I've raised with you in the past, the water pressure in Redwick. The residents of this village, just outside Newport, have suffered with low water pressure for many years due to inadequate water infrastructure serving their community. This problem is exacerbated during periods of dry weather, like the unprecedented one that we have just experienced. There are five farms in the area and the water supply problem is so bad that some farms are unable to adequately supply their dairy herds. The water supply is so low it cannot keep up with the thirst of the animals. So-called mitigation measures have been put in place, but they have fallen short, and, in some cases, failed to materialise. The only solution to this is upgrading the flow of water into the village through major infrastructure overhaul. Minister, what pressure can you bring to bear on the situation and, in particular, Dŵr Cymru, to make this happen? And what action would you expect to happen before next summer so that we don't see the same problems happening again?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Hoffwn droi at fater penodol a godais gyda chi yn y gorffennol, sef pwysedd dŵr yn Redwick. Mae trigolion y pentref hwn, sydd ar gyrion Casnewydd, wedi dioddef oherwydd pwysedd dŵr isel ers blynyddoedd lawer oherwydd seilwaith dŵr annigonol sy'n gwasanaethu eu cymuned. Mae'r broblem hon yn gwaethygu yn ystod cyfnodau o dywydd sych, fel yr un digynsail a brofwyd gennym yn ddiweddar. Mae yna bum fferm yn yr ardal ac mae'r broblem gyda'r cyflenwad dŵr mor ddifrifol fel nad yw rhai ffermydd yn gallu cyflenwi digon o ddŵr ar gyfer eu buchesi llaeth. Mae'r cyflenwad dŵr mor isel fel nad yw'n gallu diwallu syched yr anifeiliaid. Mae mesurau lliniaru honedig wedi'u rhoi ar waith, ond nid ydynt wedi bod yn ddigonol ac mewn rhai achosion, ni chawsant eu darparu o gwbl. Yr unig ateb i hyn yw gwella llif y dŵr i'r pentref drwy uwchraddio'r seilwaith yn sylweddol. Weinidog, pa bwysau y gallwch ei roi i newid y sefyllfa, ac yn benodol ar Dŵr Cymru, i sicrhau bod hyn yn digwydd? A pha gamau y byddech chi'n disgwyl eu gweld yn digwydd cyn yr haf nesaf fel na welwn yr un problemau'n digwydd eto?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, thank you for raising this issue again, in fairness. I share your concern about the problem with water pressure in Redwick and, as I say, it's something that you've raised previously. It is vitally important, first of all, of course, that people have a reliable water supply, but it's also important that farms and other businesses have the water that they need, and animal health and welfare considerations as well are essential, aren't they? So, my understanding is that Dŵr Cymru is investigating the situation and plans to update Redwick residents in October, but it is important that they assess the situation thoroughly and that the problem is addressed. This may, of course, need stages of action. There may well be short-term initial steps that they can take, but then there may be longer term requirements to plan and then implement schemes, and that will depend, of course, on what exactly the problem is and what exactly the best solution might be. But I will commit to raising this with Dŵr Cymru. I meet with them quite regularly, as it happens, and this is something that I will ask them about when we next meet.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, diolch am godi'r mater hwn eto, er tegwch. Rwy'n rhannu eich pryder am y broblem gyda phwysedd dŵr yn Redwick ac fel y dywedais, mae'n rhywbeth rydych chi wedi'i godi o'r blaen. Mae'n hanfodol bwysig, yn gyntaf oll, wrth gwrs, fod gan bobl gyflenwad dŵr dibynadwy, ond mae hefyd yn bwysig fod ffermydd a busnesau eraill yn cael y dŵr sydd ei angen arnynt, ac mae ystyriaethau iechyd a lles anifeiliaid yn allweddol hefyd, onid ydynt? Felly, fy nealltwriaeth i yw bod Dŵr Cymru yn ymchwilio i'r sefyllfa ac yn bwriadu rhoi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf i drigolion Redwick yn ystod mis Hydref, ond mae'n bwysig eu bod yn asesu'r sefyllfa'n drylwyr a bod y broblem yn cael ei datrys. Efallai y bydd angen gweithredu hyn fesul cam. Efallai'n wir y bydd camau gweithredu cychwynnol ar hyn yn y tymor byr, ond wedyn efallai y bydd gofynion mwy hirdymor i gynllunio a gweithredu cynlluniau, a bydd hynny'n dibynnu, wrth gwrs, ar beth yn union yw'r broblem a beth yn union yw'r ateb gorau. Ond rwy'n ymrwymo i godi hyn gyda Dŵr Cymru. Rwy'n cyfarfod â nhw'n eithaf rheolaidd, fel mae'n digwydd, ac mae hyn yn rhywbeth y byddaf yn gofyn iddynt yn ei gylch pan fyddwn ni'n cyfarfod nesaf.
